weeks.title: Number systems and sets
weeks.summary: Is week tum number systems (ℕ, ℤ, ℚ, ℝ) aur sets ki basic language seekhoge — union, intersection, subsets aur Venn diagram wale counting questions.
concepts: **Natural numbers (ℕ)** counting numbers hain: 0, 1, 2, 3, ... (kuch books 1 se start karti hain, isliye apne course ka convention yaad rakho). **Integers (ℤ)** me negative numbers bhi aa jaate hain.
**Rational numbers (ℚ)** wo hain jo p/q form me likhe ja sakein, jahan p, q integers aur q ≠ 0. Inka decimal ya to terminate hota hai ya repeat hota hai, jaise 0.25 ya 0.333...
**Irrational numbers** jaise √2, √7, π ka decimal na khatam hota hai na repeat hota hai. Rational aur irrational milkar **Real numbers (ℝ)** banate hain: ℕ ⊆ ℤ ⊆ ℚ ⊆ ℝ.
**Set** well-defined objects ka collection hai. Roster form me elements list karte hain {2, 4, 6}, aur set-builder form me rule likhte hain {x | x even hai, 0 < x < 8}.
**Subset**: A ⊆ B ka matlab A ka har element B me bhi hai. n elements wale set ke 2ⁿ subsets hote hain, jisme empty set ∅ aur khud wo set dono count hote hain.
**Set operations**: A ∪ B me dono sets ke saare elements, A ∩ B me sirf common elements, A − B me wo elements jo A me hain par B me nahi. Complement Aᶜ = U − A, jahan U universal set hai.
**Inclusion-exclusion**: |A ∪ B| = |A| + |B| − |A ∩ B|. Common elements do baar count ho jaate hain, isliye ek baar minus karte hain.
**Power set** P(A) matlab A ke saare subsets ka set. Agar |A| = n hai to |P(A)| = 2ⁿ.

example.problem: Ek class me 60 students hain. 35 ko Python pasand hai, 28 ko Excel pasand hai, aur 10 ko dono pasand hain. Kitne students ko dono me se kuch bhi pasand nahi hai?
steps: Maan lo P = Python wale students, E = Excel wale students. Given: |P| = 35, |E| = 28, |P ∩ E| = 10.
Kam se kam ek pasand karne wale = |P ∪ E| = |P| + |E| − |P ∩ E|.
Jinko kuch pasand nahi = total − |P ∪ E| = 60 − 53 = 7.
Answer: **7 students** ko na Python pasand hai na Excel.

mistakes: |A ∪ B| nikalte waqt sirf |A| + |B| jod dena — intersection ko minus karna mat bhoolo, warna common log do baar gin liye jaate hain.
Subsets count karte waqt empty set ∅ ya poore set ko chhod dena. Total subsets 2ⁿ hote hain; proper subsets (set khud ko chhod ke) 2ⁿ − 1.
22/7 ko irrational samajhna. 22/7 to p/q form me hai, isliye rational hai — ye sirf π ka approximation hai, π nahi.
revision: ℕ ⊆ ℤ ⊆ ℚ ⊆ ℝ; irrational = ℝ − ℚ.

questions.question: Inme se kaunsa number irrational hai?
questions.explanation: √7 kisi integer ka square nahi hai, isliye iska decimal na terminate hota hai na repeat — ye irrational hai. 0.333... = 1/3 aur √16 = 4 rational hain. 22/7 bhi rational hai; log ise π samajh kar galti karte hain.

questions.question: A = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5} aur B = {4, 5, 6, 7} hai. A − B kya hoga?
questions.explanation: A − B me wo elements aate hain jo A me hain par B me nahi: 1, 2, 3. {6, 7} to B − A hai, aur {4, 5} intersection hai. {1, 2, 3, 6, 7} symmetric difference hai, wo alag concept hai.

questions.question: Set {a, b, c, d} ke total kitne subsets hain?
questions.explanation: 4 elements hain, to subsets = 2⁴ = 16 (∅ aur poora set dono included). 15 proper subsets ki count hai — trap yahi hai. 8 = 2³ galat power hai.

questions.question: 100 logon ke survey me 45 log Hindi newspaper padhte hain, 60 English newspaper padhte hain, aur 20 dono padhte hain. Kitne log kam se kam ek newspaper padhte hain?
questions.explanation: |H ∪ E| = 45 + 60 − 20 = 85. Agar intersection minus nahi kiya to 105 aata hai, jo total logon se bhi zyada hai. 15 un logon ki count hai jo koi newspaper nahi padhte.

questions.question: Inme se kaunsa statement sahi hai?
options: Har rational number ek integer hai
Har integer ek rational number hai
questions.explanation: Koi bhi integer n ko n/1 likh sakte hain, isliye har integer rational hai (ℤ ⊆ ℚ). Ulta sahi nahi: 1/2 rational hai par integer nahi. √2 irrational hai, aur ℝ me irrationals bhi hain, isliye ℝ ⊆ ℚ galat hai.

questions.question: U = {1, 2, 3, ..., 10}. A = U ke even numbers, B = U ke multiples of 3. |(A ∪ B)ᶜ| kitna hai?
questions.explanation: A = {2, 4, 6, 8, 10}, B = {3, 6, 9}. A ∪ B = {2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 9, 10} — 7 elements (6 sirf ek baar). Complement = {1, 5, 7}, yaani 3. Agar 6 ko do baar gina to union 8 lagega aur galat answer 2 aayega; 7 to union ka size hai, complement ka nahi.

questions.question: Repeating decimal 0.272727... ko p/q form me likho.
questions.explanation: x = 0.2727... lo. Do digits repeat hote hain, to 100x = 27.2727..., aur 100x − x = 27, yaani x = 27/99 = 3/11. 27/100 to 0.27 hai jo terminate hota hai, aur 3/10 = 0.3. Repeat hone wale block ke liye 99 se divide karo, 100 se nahi.

questions.question: Set {x | x ∈ ℤ, −2 < x ≤ 3} ka roster form kya hai?
questions.explanation: −2 < x ka matlab −2 khud shamil nahi, aur x ≤ 3 ka matlab 3 shamil hai. Integers: −1, 0, 1, 2, 3. Pehla option −2 ko bhi le leta hai (< aur ≤ ka farq bhool gaye), teesra 3 ko chhod deta hai. {0, 1, 2, 3} tab aata hai jab x ∈ ℤ ko natural numbers samajh lete ho.

questions.question: Inme se kis expression ki value rational hai?
questions.explanation: √2 · √18 = √36 = 6, jo rational hai. √3 + 1 aur √5/2 me irrational number me rational jodne ya divide karne se irrational hi rehta hai, aur π/2 bhi irrational hai. Sirf √ dekh kar irrational bol dena trap hai — pehle simplify karo.

questions.question: Ek coaching ke 40 students me se har ek kam se kam ek subject — Maths ya Stats — leta hai. 25 students Maths lete hain aur 22 Stats. Kitne students dono subjects lete hain?
questions.explanation: Har student kam se kam ek subject leta hai, to |M ∪ S| = 40. Formula ulta lagao: |M ∩ S| = |M| + |S| − |M ∪ S| = 25 + 22 − 40 = 7. 47 = 25 + 22 sirf jod hai, jo total 40 se bhi zyada hai. 3 = 25 − 22 aur 15 = 40 − 25 ka is question se koi lena-dena nahi.

questions.question: U = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8}, A = {1, 2, 3, 4} aur B = {3, 4, 5, 6}. Aᶜ ∩ B kya hai?
questions.explanation: Aᶜ = U − A = {5, 6, 7, 8}. Iska B ke saath intersection = {5, 6}; ye B − A hi hai. {1, 2} = A − B hai (complement galat set ka le liya), {7, 8} = (A ∪ B)ᶜ hai, aur {3, 4} = A ∩ B.

questions.question: 80 students ki class me 48 cricket khelte hain, 35 football khelte hain, aur 12 koi bhi game nahi khelte. Kitne students exactly ek game khelte hain?
questions.explanation: Kam se kam ek game = 80 − 12 = 68. Dono = 48 + 35 − 68 = 15. Exactly ek = (kam se kam ek) − (dono) = 68 − 15 = 53. 68 'kam se kam ek' hai, exactly ek nahi — dono khelne wale isme shamil hain. 15 dono wale hain, aur 83 = 48 + 35 me common students do baar gine gaye.

questions.question: A ⊆ B hai, |A| = 2 aur |B| = 6. Kitne sets C aise hain ki A ⊆ C ⊆ B?
questions.explanation: C me A ke dono elements hona zaroori hai. B ke baaki 6 − 2 = 4 elements me se har ek ke liye do choice hain: C me ho ya na ho. Isliye 2⁴ = 16 sets (C = A aur C = B dono included). 64 = 2⁶ to B ke saare subsets hain, jinme kai A ko contain nahi karte. 15 tab aata hai jab C = A ya C = B ko chhod dete ho.

questions.question: Universal set U me 40 elements hain. A ⊆ U me 28 elements aur B ⊆ U me 20 elements hain. |A ∩ B| ki minimum possible value kya hai?
questions.explanation: |A ∪ B| = 28 + 20 − |A ∩ B|, aur A ∪ B, U ke andar hai, to |A ∪ B| ≤ 40. Isliye 48 − |A ∩ B| ≤ 40, yaani |A ∩ B| ≥ 8; jab A ∪ B = U ho to exactly 8 milta hai. 0 possible nahi, kyunki tab union 48 hota jo 40 se zyada hai. 20 maximum possible value hai (jab B ⊆ A), minimum nahi.

questions.question: Numbers √9, 0.1010010001... (har baar ek zero zyada), 3.14, √12/√3, π − 1 aur √2 + √8 me se kitne irrational hain?
questions.explanation: √9 = 3, 3.14 = 314/100 aur √12/√3 = √4 = 2 — ye teeno rational hain. 0.1010010001... me zeros ka block badhta jaata hai, to decimal kabhi repeat nahi hota: irrational. π − 1 irrational, aur √2 + √8 = √2 + 2√2 = 3√2 bhi irrational. Total 3. 3.14 ko π samajhna ya √12/√3 ko simplify na karna 4 ya 5 tak le jaata hai.

weeks.title: Relations and functions
weeks.summary: Cartesian product se relations banana, reflexive/symmetric/transitive check karna, aur samajhna ki function ek special relation kyun hai.
concepts: **Cartesian product** A × B = saare ordered pairs (a, b) jahan a ∈ A, b ∈ B. |A × B| = |A| · |B|, aur (a, b) ≠ (b, a) generally.
**Relation** A se B tak = A × B ka koi bhi subset. Set A par relation matlab A × A ka subset; n elements wale set par 2^(n²) relations possible hain.
**Reflexive**: har a ke liye (a, a) ∈ R. **Symmetric**: (a, b) ∈ R ho to (b, a) ∈ R bhi. **Transitive**: (a, b) aur (b, c) ∈ R ho to (a, c) ∈ R.

**Equivalence relation** = reflexive + symmetric + transitive. Ye set ko alag-alag **equivalence classes** me tod deta hai, jaise integers ko '3 se divide karne par remainder' ke hisaab se 3 groups me.
**Function** f: A → B ek relation hai jisme A ke har element ka exactly ek image ho. Ek input ke do output hon, ya koi input chhoot jaye, to function nahi.
**Domain, codomain, range**: domain = allowed inputs, codomain = jahan outputs aa sakte hain, range = jo outputs actually aate hain. Hamesha range ⊆ codomain.

example.problem: A = {1, 2, 3} par R = {(1,1), (2,2), (3,3), (1,2), (2,1)}. Check karo R equivalence relation hai ya nahi, aur equivalence classes likho.
steps: Reflexive: (1,1), (2,2), (3,3) teeno R me hain, to R reflexive hai.
Symmetric: (1,2) hai to (2,1) bhi hai; baaki pairs (a,a) type ke hain. To R symmetric hai.
Transitive: (1,2) aur (2,1) se (1,1) chahiye — hai. (2,1) aur (1,2) se (2,2) chahiye — hai. (a,a) wale pairs se kuch naya nahi banta. To R transitive hai.
Teeno properties hold karti hain, isliye R equivalence relation hai.
Classes: 1 aur 2 ek doosre se related hain, 3 sirf khud se. Answer: classes **{1, 2}** aur **{3}**.

mistakes: Symmetric check karte waqt sirf ek pair dekhna. Har (a, b) ke liye (b, a) check karo.
Codomain aur range ko same samajhna. f(x) = x² on ℤ → ℤ ka codomain ℤ hai, par range sirf perfect squares hai.
Ek input ke do outputs wale relation ko function maan lena — function me har input ka exactly ek output hona chahiye.
revision: n elements par relations ki count = 2^(n²).
Function: har input ka exactly ek output.

questions.question: A = {1, 2} aur B = {x, y, z}. |A × B| kitna hai?
questions.explanation: |A × B| = |A| · |B| = 2 · 3 = 6 ordered pairs. 5 tab aata hai jab galti se sizes ko jod dete hain — product ke liye multiply karna hota hai.

questions.question: Inme se kaunsa relation {1, 2, 3} se {a, b} tak function NAHI hai?
questions.explanation: Teesre option me input 1 ke do outputs hain (a aur b), isliye ye function nahi hai. Pehla option bhi valid function hai — saare inputs ka same output hona allowed hai, bas har input ka ek hi output ho.

questions.question: ℤ par relation R: a R b agar (a − b) 5 se divisible ho. R kis type ka hai?
options: Reflexive aur symmetric, par transitive nahi
questions.explanation: a − a = 0 divisible by 5 (reflexive). a − b divisible ho to b − a = −(a − b) bhi (symmetric). a − b aur b − c dono divisible hon to unka sum a − c bhi divisible (transitive). Isliye equivalence relation; transitive ko check kiye bina chhod dena common trap hai.

questions.question: ℝ par relation R: a R b agar a ≤ b. Inme se kaunsi property R me fail hoti hai?
questions.explanation: a ≤ a hamesha sach (reflexive), a ≤ b aur b ≤ c se a ≤ c (transitive). Par 2 ≤ 5 hai, 5 ≤ 2 nahi — isliye symmetric fail hota hai.

questions.question: f: ℤ → ℤ, f(x) = x². Is function ki range kya hai?
questions.explanation: Integer ka square hamesha perfect square hota hai: 0, 1, 4, 9, ... 'Saare non-negative integers' trap hai, kyunki 2 ya 3 kabhi output nahi aate. Codomain ℤ hai, par range usse chhoti hai.

questions.question: 3 elements wale set A par total kitne alag relations ban sakte hain?
questions.explanation: Relation on A = A × A ka subset. |A × A| = 3 · 3 = 9, isliye subsets = 2⁹ = 512. 9 sirf pairs ki count hai, relations ki nahi; 64 = 2⁶ tab aata hai jab galti se 3 + 3 = 6 pairs maan lete hain.

questions.question: Agar ordered pairs (x + 1, 4) aur (3, y − 2) equal hain, to x aur y kya hain?
questions.explanation: Do ordered pairs tabhi equal hote hain jab pehle components equal hon aur doosre bhi: x + 1 = 3 se x = 2, aur y − 2 = 4 se y = 6. y = 2 tab aata hai jab −2 ko doosri side le jaate waqt sign nahi badalte. x = 3, y = 4 me components ko seedha copy kar diya.

questions.question: f: {1, 2, 3, 4} → {1, 2, ..., 10}, f(x) = 2x + 1. Is function ki range kya hai?
questions.explanation: Range = jo outputs actually aate hain: f(1) = 3, f(2) = 5, f(3) = 7, f(4) = 9, to range {3, 5, 7, 9}. {1, 2, ..., 10} codomain hai, range nahi, aur {1, 2, 3, 4} domain hai. {2, 4, 6, 8} me + 1 bhool gaye.

questions.question: A = {1, 2, 3} par relation R = {(1, 1), (2, 2), (1, 3), (3, 1)} hai. R ko reflexive banane ke liye kaunsa pair add karna zaroori hai?
questions.explanation: Reflexive ke liye A ke har a ke liye (a, a) chahiye: (1, 1) aur (2, 2) hain, par (3, 3) missing hai. Baaki pairs (2, 1), (1, 2), (2, 3) reflexive hone ke liye zaroori nahi — reflexive sirf diagonal pairs (a, a) ki baat karta hai.

questions.question: A = {p, q} aur B = {1, 2, 3}. A se B tak kitne alag functions ban sakte hain?
questions.explanation: Function me A ke har element ka exactly ek image chahiye. p ke liye 3 choices, q ke liye bhi 3 choices, to 3 · 3 = 3² = 9 functions. 8 = 2³ tab aata hai jab base aur power ulta kar dete ho. 64 = 2⁶ A se B tak saare relations hain, functions nahi, aur 6 = |A × B| sirf pairs ki count hai.

questions.question: Set {1, 2, ..., 10} par relation R: a R b agar (a − b) 4 se divisible ho. 2 ki equivalence class kya hai?
questions.explanation: 2 ki class me wo saare b aate hain jinke liye 2 − b, 4 se divisible ho, yaani b ko 4 se divide karne par remainder 2 aaye: 2, 6, 10. {2, 4, 6, 8, 10} saare even numbers hain — 4 − 2 = 2, 4 se divisible nahi. {6, 10} me 2 khud chhoot gaya, jabki reflexive hone ki wajah se 2 R 2 hamesha sach hai.

questions.question: A = {1, 2, 3, 4} par R = {(1, 1), (2, 2), (3, 3), (4, 4), (1, 2), (2, 1), (2, 3), (3, 2)}. R ke baare me kya sahi hai?
questions.explanation: Saare (a, a) maujood hain, to reflexive. (1, 2) ke saath (2, 1) aur (2, 3) ke saath (3, 2) bhi hai, to symmetric. Par (1, 2) aur (2, 3) dono R me hain jabki (1, 3) nahi — transitive fail. Isliye ye equivalence relation nahi hai. Sirf pehli do properties check karke 'equivalence' bol dena main trap hai.

questions.question: Set {a, b, c} par kitne relations aise hain jo reflexive aur symmetric dono hon?
questions.explanation: Reflexive ke liye (a, a), (b, b), (c, c) teeno hona zaroori hai — inme koi choice nahi. Symmetric ke liye off-diagonal pairs jodi me aate hain: {(a, b), (b, a)}, {(a, c), (c, a)}, {(b, c), (c, b)} — har jodi ya to poori aayegi ya bilkul nahi. 3 jodiyan, har ek ki 2 choices: 2³ = 8. 64 = 2⁶ sirf reflexive relations hain (symmetry ignore ki), aur 512 = 2⁹ saare relations.

questions.question: A × B me exactly 6 elements hain, aur (1, x), (2, y), (3, x) inme shamil hain (x ≠ y). Inme se kaunsa pair A × B me zaroor hoga?
questions.explanation: Given pairs se A me kam se kam 1, 2, 3 hain aur B me kam se kam x, y. Tab |A × B| ≥ 3 · 2 = 6, aur ye exactly 6 hai, to A = {1, 2, 3} aur B = {x, y} hi hone chahiye. Isliye (2, x) zaroor hai. (x, 2) aur (y, 1) me order ulta hai — pehla component A se aata hai. 4, A me ho hi nahi sakta, warna 8 elements ho jaate.

questions.question: ℤ par relation R: a R b agar a + b even ho. R ke baare me kya sahi hai?
options: Equivalence relation hai, jiski 2 equivalence classes hain
Reflexive aur symmetric hai, par transitive nahi
Equivalence relation hai, jiski infinitely many classes hain
questions.explanation: a + a = 2a hamesha even, to reflexive. a + b = b + a, to symmetric. Agar a + b aur b + c even hain, to a + c = (a + b) + (b + c) − 2b bhi even — transitive. a + b even tabhi hota hai jab a, b dono even ya dono odd hon, isliye sirf 2 classes: even integers aur odd integers. 'a + a odd ho sakta hai' wali soch galat hai, aur transitive ko bina check kiye fail maan lena bhi trap hai.

weeks.title: Coordinate geometry: straight lines
weeks.summary: Points ke beech distance, midpoint, slope, line ki equation, aur parallel/perpendicular lines ki conditions.
concepts: **Distance formula**: P(x₁, y₁) aur Q(x₂, y₂) ke beech distance = √((x₂ − x₁)² + (y₂ − y₁)²). Ye Pythagoras theorem hi hai.
**Section formula**: segment ko m:n me internally divide karne wala point = ((m·x₂ + n·x₁)/(m + n), (m·y₂ + n·y₁)/(m + n)). m:n = 1:1 lo to **midpoint** milta hai.
**Slope** m = (y₂ − y₁)/(x₂ − x₁) = tan θ. Horizontal line ka slope 0, vertical line ka slope undefined.
**Parallel** lines ke slopes equal: m₁ = m₂. **Perpendicular** lines me m₁ · m₂ = −1 (agar koi vertical/horizontal na ho).
**Line ke forms**: slope-intercept y = mx + c, point-slope y − y₁ = m(x − x₁), general form ax + by + c = 0 jiska slope −a/b hota hai.
**Intercepts**: x-intercept ke liye y = 0 rakho, y-intercept ke liye x = 0 rakho.
**Point se line ki distance**: (x₀, y₀) se ax + by + c = 0 tak perpendicular distance = |a·x₀ + b·y₀ + c| / √(a² + b²).

example.problem: Points (2, 3) aur (4, 7) se guzarne wali line ki equation aur uske intercepts nikalo.
steps: Point-slope form with (2, 3): y − 3 = 2(x − 2).
Simplify: y = 2x − 4 + 3 = 2x − 1.
y-intercept: x = 0 rakho, y = −1. x-intercept: y = 0 rakho, 2x = 1, x = 1/2.
Answer: **y = 2x − 1** (general form 2x − y − 1 = 0), x-intercept 1/2, y-intercept −1.

mistakes: Slope me order mix karna, jaise (y₂ − y₁)/(x₁ − x₂). Numerator aur denominator me same point pehle lo.
ax + by + c = 0 ka slope a/b likh dena — sahi slope −a/b hai.
Perpendicular slope ko 1/m likhna. Sahi hai −1/m (sign bhi badalta hai).
revision: Slope = (y₂ − y₁)/(x₂ − x₁); ax + by + c = 0 ka slope −a/b.
Parallel: m₁ = m₂; perpendicular: m₁ · m₂ = −1.

questions.question: Points (1, 2) aur (4, 6) ke beech distance kitna hai?
questions.explanation: √((4 − 1)² + (6 − 2)²) = √(9 + 16) = √25 = 5. 25 tab aata hai jab square root lena bhool jaate hain; 7 = 3 + 4 seedha jod dene se aata hai, jo galat hai.

questions.question: Line 3x + 4y − 12 = 0 ka slope kya hai?
questions.explanation: 4y = −3x + 12, to y = −(3/4)x + 3, slope = −3/4. Formula −a/b se bhi −3/4 aata hai. Minus sign bhoolne par 3/4 aata hai, aur a/b ulta karne par −4/3.

questions.question: Line y = 2x + 5 ke perpendicular aur point (0, 1) se guzarne wali line kaunsi hai?
questions.explanation: Given slope 2 hai, perpendicular slope = −1/2. (0, 1) se guzarti hai to y-intercept 1: y = −x/2 + 1. y = 2x + 1 parallel line hai; y = x/2 + 1 me sign change karna bhool gaye.

questions.question: A(1, 2) aur B(7, 8) ko jodne wale segment ko A ki taraf se 1:2 ratio me internally divide karne wala point kaunsa hai?
questions.explanation: m:n = 1:2, point = ((1·7 + 2·1)/3, (1·8 + 2·2)/3) = (9/3, 12/3) = (3, 4). Ye A ke paas hona chahiye kyunki A se distance kam hai. (5, 6) ratio ulta lagane par aata hai, aur (4, 5) midpoint hai.

questions.question: Lines 2x + ky = 5 aur 4x + 6y = 7 parallel hain. k ki value kya hai?
questions.explanation: Slopes: −2/k aur −4/6 = −2/3. Parallel ke liye −2/k = −2/3, to k = 3. Check: 2x + 3y = 5 ko 2 se multiply karo to 4x + 6y = 10 — same direction, alag line. −3 sign galti se aata hai.

questions.question: Point (3, −2) se line 4x − 3y + 2 = 0 ki perpendicular distance kitni hai?
questions.explanation: |4·3 − 3·(−2) + 2| / √(4² + 3²) = |12 + 6 + 2| / 5 = 20/5 = 4. −3 · (−2) = +6 hota hai; yahan sign galat karne par 8/5 aata hai. Denominator √(a² + b²) bhoolne par 20 aata hai.

questions.question: Points (−3, 5) aur (7, −1) ka midpoint kya hai?
questions.explanation: Midpoint = ((−3 + 7)/2, (5 + (−1))/2) = (4/2, 4/2) = (2, 2). (4, 4) me coordinates jod to diye par 2 se divide karna bhool gaye. (10, −6) coordinates ka difference hai, aur (5, −3) us difference ka aadha — midpoint me jodna hota hai, ghataana nahi.

questions.question: Points (2, −1) aur (5, 8) se guzarne wali line ka slope kya hai?
questions.explanation: Slope = (8 − (−1))/(5 − 2) = 9/3 = 3. 7/3 tab aata hai jab −(−1) ko −1 likh dete ho. 1/3 me x aur y ka difference ulta rakh diya, aur −3 tab aata hai jab numerator me ek point pehle aur denominator me doosra point pehle le lete ho.

questions.question: Line 2x − 5y + 10 = 0 ka y-intercept kya hai?
questions.explanation: y-intercept ke liye x = 0 rakho: −5y + 10 = 0, to y = 2. −5 x-intercept hai (y = 0 rakhne par 2x + 10 = 0, x = −5). −2 sign ki galti hai, aur 10 sirf constant term hai, intercept nahi.

questions.question: Points (1, 2), (3, 6) aur (k, 10) ek hi line par hain (collinear). k ki value kya hai?
questions.explanation: Pehle do points ka slope = (6 − 2)/(3 − 1) = 2. Teesra point bhi isi line par hai, to (10 − 2)/(k − 1) = 2, yaani k − 1 = 4 aur k = 5. 4 tab aata hai jab k − 1 = 4 ko hi answer maan lete ho. 17 slope ko ulta (Δx/Δy) lene par aata hai, aur −3 tab jab denominator me order ulta karke (1 − k) likh dete ho.

questions.question: Lines 3x − 2y + 4 = 0 aur kx + 6y − 1 = 0 ek doosre ke perpendicular hain. k ki value kya hai?
questions.explanation: Slopes −a/b se: pehli line ka 3/2, doosri ka −k/6. Perpendicular ke liye (3/2)(−k/6) = −1, yaani −k/4 = −1 aur k = 4. −9 parallel lines ki condition (−k/6 = 3/2) se aata hai. −4 tab aata hai jab pehli line ka slope −3/2 le lete ho (−a/b me sign galat).

questions.question: Points A(1, 3) aur B(5, 7) ko jodne wale segment ka perpendicular bisector kaunsa hai?
questions.explanation: Perpendicular bisector midpoint se guzarta hai aur AB ke perpendicular hota hai. Midpoint = (3, 5), AB ka slope = (7 − 3)/(5 − 1) = 1, to perpendicular slope = −1. y − 5 = −(x − 3) ⇒ x + y = 8. y = x + 2 khud line AB hai. x + y = 4 aur x + y = 12 slope sahi rakhti hain par A ya B se guzarti hain, midpoint se nahi.

questions.question: Parallel lines 3x + 4y − 7 = 0 aur 6x + 8y + 6 = 0 ke beech ki distance kitni hai?
questions.explanation: Pehli line par ek point lo: (1, 1), kyunki 3 + 4 − 7 = 0. Iski doosri line se distance = |6·1 + 8·1 + 6| / √(6² + 8²) = 20/10 = 2. Ya doosri line ko 2 se divide karo (3x + 4y + 3 = 0), phir |−7 − 3|/5 = 2. 13/5 tab aata hai jab coefficients same kiye bina |−7 − 6|/5 le lete ho; 4/5 me sign galat ho gaya, aur 10 me √(a² + b²) se divide karna bhool gaye.

questions.question: Point P(4, y), A(2, −3) aur B(8, 6) ko jodne wale segment par hai. P is segment ko A ki taraf se kis ratio me divide karta hai, aur y kya hai?
questions.explanation: Ratio m:n maano. x-coordinate: (8m + 2n)/(m + n) = 4 ⇒ 8m + 2n = 4m + 4n ⇒ 4m = 2n ⇒ m:n = 1:2. Ab y = (1·6 + 2·(−3))/3 = 0. 2:1 tab aata hai jab section formula me m aur n ki jagah ulti kar dete ho. 1:1 midpoint maan lena hai, par midpoint ka x-coordinate 5 hai, 4 nahi. '1:2 aur y = 3' me ratio sahi hai par y nikalte waqt weights ulte lag gaye.

questions.question: Line x + y = 1 me point (3, 4) ka mirror image (reflection) kya hai?
questions.explanation: (3, 4) se line ke perpendicular jaao: line ka slope −1 hai, to perpendicular slope 1: y = x + 1. Isko x + y = 1 ke saath solve karo: x = 0, y = 1, to foot (0, 1). Foot image aur (3, 4) ka midpoint hai, to image = (2·0 − 3, 2·1 − 4) = (−3, −2). Check: midpoint (0, 1) line par hai ✓. (0, 1) sirf foot hai, image nahi. (−4, −3) line x + y = 0 me reflection hai (+1 bhool gaye), aur (−2, −3) me coordinates ulte lag gaye.

weeks.title: Quadratic functions
weeks.summary: Parabola ka shape, vertex, discriminant se roots ka nature, aur roots ke sum-product formulas.
concepts: **Quadratic function**: f(x) = ax² + bx + c, jahan a ≠ 0. Iska graph ek **parabola** hota hai.
a > 0 ho to parabola upar khulta hai aur vertex pe **minimum** value milti hai; a < 0 ho to neeche khulta hai aur vertex pe **maximum**.
**Vertex** ka x-coordinate = −b/(2a). Isi se guzarne wali vertical line x = −b/(2a) **axis of symmetry** hai.
**Discriminant** D = b² − 4ac. D > 0: do alag real roots; D = 0: ek repeated root (graph x-axis ko touch karta hai); D < 0: koi real root nahi.
**Quadratic formula**: x = (−b ± √D) / (2a).
**Roots ka sum aur product**: α + β = −b/a, αβ = c/a.
**Vertex form**: f(x) = a(x − h)² + k, jahan vertex (h, k) hai. Completing the square se ye form milta hai.

example.problem: f(x) = x² − 6x + 5 ka vertex, minimum value aur roots nikalo.
steps: a = 1, b = −6, c = 5. a > 0 hai, to parabola upar khulega aur vertex pe minimum hoga.
Vertex x = −b/(2a) = 6/2 = 3.
f(3) = 9 − 18 + 5 = −4, to vertex (3, −4) aur vertex form (x − 3)² − 4.
D = 36 − 20 = 16 > 0, to do alag real roots.
x = (6 ± 4)/2, yaani x = 5 ya x = 1.
Answer: vertex **(3, −4)**, minimum value **−4**, roots **1 aur 5**.

mistakes: Vertex formula me sign galat lena: x = −b/(2a) hai, b/(2a) nahi.
Max/min value poochi ho to vertex ka x-coordinate likh dena — value ke liye us x ko f(x) me rakhna padta hai.
Product of roots ko −c/a likhna. Sahi hai c/a; sum me minus aata hai (−b/a).
revision: D = b² − 4ac: >0 do roots, =0 ek root, <0 no real root.

questions.question: f(x) = 2x² − 8x + 3 ke vertex ka x-coordinate kya hai?
questions.explanation: x = −b/(2a) = −(−8)/(2·2) = 8/4 = 2. Minus sign chhod dene par −2 aata hai, aur 2a ki jagah sirf a se divide karne par 4.

questions.question: Equation x² + 4x + 7 = 0 ke roots ke baare me kya sahi hai?
options: Ek positive aur ek negative root
questions.explanation: D = 4² − 4·1·7 = 16 − 28 = −12 < 0, isliye koi real root nahi; parabola poora x-axis ke upar hai. Sirf b² positive dekh kar 'do roots' bol dena galat hai — 4ac bhi subtract karna padta hai.

questions.question: f(x) = −x² + 4x + 1 ki maximum value kya hai?
questions.explanation: a = −1 < 0, to vertex pe maximum. x = −4/(2·(−1)) = 2, f(2) = −4 + 8 + 1 = 5. 2 to sirf vertex ka x-coordinate hai, value nahi. −11 tab aata hai jab x = −2 rakh dete ho.

questions.question: Agar α, β equation 2x² − 5x + 3 = 0 ke roots hain, to α + β aur αβ kya hain?
questions.explanation: α + β = −b/a = 5/2, αβ = c/a = 3/2. Check: roots 1 aur 3/2 hain, sum 5/2 aur product 3/2 ✓. Sum me minus bhoolne se −5/2, aur a = 2 se divide na karne par 5 aur 3 aata hai.

questions.question: Equation x² + kx + 9 = 0 ke equal roots hain aur k > 0. k kya hai?
questions.explanation: Equal roots ke liye D = 0: k² − 36 = 0, to k = ±6; k > 0 hai isliye k = 6. 36 = k² hai, k nahi. Tab equation (x + 3)² = 0 banti hai.

questions.question: Ek parabola ka vertex (1, −2) hai aur ye point (3, 6) se guzarta hai. Iski equation kya hai?
questions.explanation: Vertex form: f(x) = a(x − 1)² − 2. (3, 6) rakho: 4a − 2 = 6, to a = 2. f(x) = 2(x − 1)² − 2 = 2x² − 4x. Option 1 me a = 1 maan liya (a nikala hi nahi). 2x² + 4x me (x + 1) liya, yaani vertex ka sign galat.

questions.question: f(x) = −2x² + 3x + 5 ka graph kaisa hai?
options: Upar khulta hai aur vertex pe minimum hai
Neeche khulta hai aur vertex pe maximum hai
Upar khulta hai aur vertex pe maximum hai
Neeche khulta hai aur iski koi maximum value nahi hai
questions.explanation: Shape sirf x² ke coefficient a se decide hota hai. Yahan a = −2 < 0, to parabola neeche khulta hai aur vertex sabse ooncha point hai — wahan maximum. +3x aur +5 dekh kar 'upar khulta hai' bolna galat hai. Neeche khulne wale parabola ki maximum value hamesha hoti hai: vertex pe.

questions.question: Equation x² − 5x − 14 = 0 ke roots kya hain?
questions.explanation: Aise do numbers chahiye jinka product −14 aur sum −5 ho: −7 aur 2. To x² − 5x − 14 = (x − 7)(x + 2), aur roots x = 7, x = −2. Check: 49 − 35 − 14 = 0 ✓. '−7, 2' me factors ke numbers ko hi roots likh diya — roots ka sign factors se ulta hota hai. 7, 2 ka product 14 hai, −14 nahi.

questions.question: Equation 4x² − 12x + 9 = 0 ke roots ke baare me kya sahi hai?
questions.explanation: D = (−12)² − 4·4·9 = 144 − 144 = 0, to ek repeated root: x = −b/(2a) = 12/8 = 3/2. Ye (2x − 3)² = 0 hai. x = 3 tab aata hai jab 2a ki jagah sirf a se divide karte ho. D = 0 ka matlab 'koi root nahi' nahi hai — graph x-axis ko touch karta hai.

questions.question: Completing the square se f(x) = x² + 6x + 11 ko vertex form me likho. Vertex kya hai?
questions.explanation: x² + 6x = (x + 3)² − 9, to f(x) = (x + 3)² − 9 + 11 = (x + 3)² + 2. Vertex form a(x − h)² + k se h = −3, k = 2: vertex (−3, 2). (3, 2) me (x + 3) ko x − 3 samajh liya. (−3, 11) me −9 adjust karna bhool gaye, aur (−6, 11) me −b/a liya, −b/(2a) nahi.

questions.question: Equation x² + px − 12 = 0 ka ek root 3 hai. Doosra root kya hai?
questions.explanation: Product of roots = c/a = −12, to 3 · β = −12 aur β = −4. Ya x = 3 rakho: 9 + 3p − 12 = 0, p = 1; sum = −p = −1 = 3 + β, phir bhi β = −4. 4 tab aata hai jab product ko +12 le lete ho. 1 to p ki value hai, aur −1 roots ka sum hai, doosra root nahi.

questions.question: k ki kin values ke liye equation x² − 2kx + 9 = 0 ka koi real root nahi hai?
questions.explanation: No real root ke liye D < 0: (−2k)² − 4·1·9 = 4k² − 36 < 0 ⇒ k² < 9 ⇒ −3 < k < 3. 'k < −3 ya k > 3' to D > 0 ki condition hai (do alag roots). 'k > 3' me sirf positive square root socha. −6 < k < 6 tab aata hai jab b ko k le lete ho, −2k nahi.

questions.question: Agar α, β equation x² − 4x + 1 = 0 ke roots hain, to α² + β² kya hai?
questions.explanation: α + β = −b/a = 4 aur αβ = c/a = 1. α² + β² = (α + β)² − 2αβ = 16 − 2 = 14. 16 tab aata hai jab α² + β² ko (α + β)² maan lete ho; 18 me −2αβ ki jagah +2αβ laga diya. Roots 2 ± √3 nikal ke bhi check kar sakte ho: (7 + 4√3) + (7 − 4√3) = 14 ✓.

questions.question: Ek kisaan ke paas 60 m fencing hai. Wo ek seedhi deewar ke saath rectangular khet banata hai, to fencing sirf teen sides par lagti hai (deewar chauthi side hai). Khet ka maximum possible area kitna hai (m² me)?
questions.explanation: Deewar ke perpendicular wali do sides x lo; deewar ke parallel wali side = 60 − 2x. Area A(x) = x(60 − 2x) = −2x² + 60x, jo a < 0 wala quadratic hai. Vertex x = −60/(2·(−2)) = 15, to A = 15 · 30 = 450. 225 tab aata hai jab khet ko 15 × 15 square maan lete ho (chaaron sides par fencing). 900 tab jab x(60 − x) le lete ho, aur 15 to sirf x hai, area nahi.

questions.question: Ek quadratic function ke roots 2 aur −3 hain, aur iska graph point (0, 12) se guzarta hai. Iske vertex ka y-coordinate kya hai?
questions.explanation: f(x) = a(x − 2)(x + 3). f(0) = a(−2)(3) = −6a = 12, to a = −2. Vertex roots ke beech me hai: x = (2 + (−3))/2 = −1/2. f(−1/2) = −2(−5/2)(5/2) = 25/2. −25/2 tab aata hai jab a = 2 le lete ho (sign galti). 12 to y-intercept hai, aur −1/2 vertex ka x-coordinate.

weeks.title: Algebra of polynomials
weeks.summary: Polynomials ka degree, operations, division algorithm, remainder aur factor theorem, aur roots se graph ka behaviour.
concepts: **Polynomial**: aₙxⁿ + ... + a₁x + a₀, jahan saari powers non-negative integers hain. Sabse badi power = **degree**, aur uska coefficient = **leading coefficient**.
1/x, √x jaise terms polynomial me allowed nahi, par coefficients koi bhi real number ho sakte hain (jaise √3·x²).
**Operations**: addition/subtraction me like terms combine karo. Multiplication me degrees jud jaati hain: deg(p·q) = deg p + deg q.
**Division algorithm**: p(x) = d(x)·q(x) + r(x), jahan r = 0 ya deg r < deg d.
**Remainder theorem**: p(x) ko (x − a) se divide karo to remainder = p(a). (x + a) ke liye p(−a) rakho.
**Factor theorem**: p(a) = 0 ho tabhi (x − a), p(x) ka factor hota hai. Degree n polynomial ke at most n real roots hote hain.
**Graph behaviour**: odd multiplicity root pe graph x-axis cross karta hai, even multiplicity pe touch karke wapas mudta hai. Leading term se pata chalta hai ki dono ends upar jaayenge ya neeche.

steps: Constant term −6 ke factors try karo: ±1, ±2, ±3, ±6.
p(1) = 1 − 6 + 11 − 6 = 0, to factor theorem se (x − 1) factor hai.
Divide karo: p(x) = (x − 1)(x² − 5x + 6).
Check: (x − 1)(x² − 5x + 6) = x³ − 5x² + 6x − x² + 5x − 6 = x³ − 6x² + 11x − 6 ✓.

mistakes: (x + a) se divide karte waqt p(a) rakh dena. Remainder p(−a) hota hai, kyunki x + a = x − (−a).
Subtraction me doosre bracket ke har term ka sign badalna bhool jaana.
Product ki degree ko degrees ka multiplication samajhna — degrees add hoti hain.
revision: Degree n ⇒ at most n real roots, at most n − 1 turning points.
Even multiplicity: touch; odd multiplicity: cross.

questions.question: Inme se kaunsa polynomial NAHI hai?
questions.explanation: 2/x = 2x⁻¹, jisme power negative hai, isliye x² + 2/x polynomial nahi. Constant 5 degree 0 ka polynomial hai, aur √3·x² me sirf coefficient irrational hai — power to 2 hi hai, wo allowed hai.

questions.question: (x³ + 2x)(4x² − 1) ki degree kya hai?
questions.explanation: Leading terms ka product x³ · 4x² = 4x⁵, isliye degree 3 + 2 = 5. 6 tab aata hai jab degrees ko multiply kar dete ho.

questions.question: p(x) = 2x³ − 3x² + x − 5 ko (x + 1) se divide karne par remainder kya hoga?
questions.explanation: (x + 1) ke liye x = −1 rakho: 2(−1) − 3(1) + (−1) − 5 = −2 − 3 − 1 − 5 = −11. −5 to p(1) hai, jo (x − 1) se divide karne par aata.

questions.question: Agar (x − 2), x³ − kx + 6 ka factor hai, to k kya hai?
questions.explanation: Factor theorem: p(2) = 0. 8 − 2k + 6 = 0, to 2k = 14, k = 7. Galti se x = −2 rakhne par −8 + 2k + 6 = 0, k = 1 aata hai — trap yahi hai.

questions.question: (x² + 3x − 1) − (2x² − x + 4) ko simplify karo.
questions.explanation: Doosre bracket ka har sign badlo: x² + 3x − 1 − 2x² + x − 4 = −x² + 4x − 5. Agar minus sirf pehle term pe lagaya to −x² + 2x + 3 aata hai — ye sabse common galti hai.

questions.question: p(x) = (x + 1)²(x − 2)(x − 3). Diye gaye x values me se kis par p(x) < 0 hai?
questions.explanation: (x + 1)² kabhi negative nahi hota, to sign (x − 2)(x − 3) se decide hota hai, jo sirf 2 < x < 3 me negative hai. x = 2.5: (3.5)²(0.5)(−0.5) < 0 ✓. x = −2 par p = 1·(−4)(−5) = 20 > 0 — −1 even multiplicity root hai, wahan sign nahi badalta.

questions.question: Polynomial 7 − 3x² + 5x⁴ − x ki degree aur leading coefficient kya hain?
questions.explanation: Sabse badi power x⁴ hai, to degree 4, aur uska coefficient 5 leading coefficient hai. 7 sirf pehle likha hua term (constant) hai — leading coefficient likhne ke order se nahi, sabse badi power se decide hota hai. 'Degree 5, leading coefficient 4' me power aur coefficient ulte ho gaye.

questions.question: p(x) = x³ − 2x² + 4 ko (x − 3) se divide karne par remainder kya hoga?
questions.explanation: Remainder theorem: (x − 3) ke liye p(3) nikalo: 27 − 18 + 4 = 13. −41 = p(−3) hai, jo (x + 3) se divide karne par aata. 49 tab aata hai jab −2x² ko +18 le lete ho, aur 4 sirf constant term hai.

questions.question: Degree 5 wale polynomial ke graph me at most kitne turning points ho sakte hain?
questions.explanation: Degree n polynomial ke at most n − 1 turning points hote hain, to 5 − 1 = 4. 5 to real roots ki maximum count hai, turning points ki nahi. 'At most' ka matlab hai kam bhi ho sakte hain (jaise x⁵ me koi turning point nahi), par 4 se zyada kabhi nahi.

questions.question: (2x² − x + 3)(x² + 4x − 1) ko expand karne par x² ka coefficient kya hoga?
questions.explanation: x² teen tarah se banta hai: 2x² · (−1) = −2x², (−x) · 4x = −4x², aur 3 · x² = 3x². Total −2 − 4 + 3 = −3. 5 tab aata hai jab (−x)(4x) ko +4x² le lete ho. −6 me 3 · x² wala term chhoot gaya — har pair check karo jiski powers jud kar 2 banti hain.

questions.question: 2x³ − 3x² + 4x − 1 ko (x − 1) se divide karne par quotient kya aata hai?
questions.explanation: Synthetic division with 1: coefficients 2, −3, 4, −1 → 2; 2·1 − 3 = −1; −1·1 + 4 = 3; 3·1 − 1 = 2. Quotient 2x² − x + 3, remainder 2. Check: (x − 1)(2x² − x + 3) + 2 = 2x³ − 3x² + 4x − 1 ✓. 2x² − 5x + 9 tab aata hai jab 1 ki jagah −1 se divide karte ho, yaani (x + 1) ka quotient.

questions.question: p(x) = x³ + ax² + bx − 6. (x − 1), p(x) ka factor hai, aur p(x) ko (x + 1) se divide karne par remainder 4 aata hai. a aur b kya hain?
questions.explanation: Factor theorem: p(1) = 1 + a + b − 6 = 0 ⇒ a + b = 5. Remainder theorem: p(−1) = −1 + a − b − 6 = 4 ⇒ a − b = 11. Jodne par 2a = 16, a = 8, b = −3. 'a = 6, b = −1' tab aata hai jab p(−1) = 0 le lete ho (remainder 4 ignore). 'a = 8, b = 1' me dono conditions ulti lag gayi, aur 'a = −3, b = 8' me a, b swap ho gaye.

questions.question: Ek cubic polynomial p(x) ke roots 1, −2 aur 3 hain, aur p(0) = 12 hai. p(2) kya hai?
questions.explanation: Factor theorem se p(x) = a(x − 1)(x + 2)(x − 3). p(0) = a(−1)(2)(−3) = 6a = 12, to a = 2. p(2) = 2(1)(4)(−1) = −8. −4 tab aata hai jab a = 1 maan lete ho (p(0) wali condition use hi nahi ki). 8 me (2 − 3) = −1 ka sign chhoot gaya, aur 12 to p(0) hai.

questions.question: Polynomial p(x) ko (x − 2) se divide karne par remainder 5 aata hai, aur (x + 1) se divide karne par remainder −1. p(x) ko (x − 2)(x + 1) se divide karne par remainder kya hoga?
questions.explanation: Divisor ki degree 2 hai, to remainder r(x) = mx + c (degree < 2). p(x) = (x − 2)(x + 1)q(x) + mx + c. x = 2 rakho: 2m + c = 5; x = −1 rakho: −m + c = −1. Ghataane par 3m = 6, m = 2, c = 1: remainder 2x + 1. x + 3 sirf pehli condition (x = 2 par 5) satisfy karta hai, x = −1 par 2 deta hai. 4 = 5 + (−1) aur −5 = 5 · (−1) remainders ko jodna/multiply karna hai, jo sahi tarika nahi.

questions.question: p(x) = −(x + 1)²(x − 3) ke baare me kaunsa statement sahi hai?
options: x = −1 par graph x-axis ko cross karta hai
x = 3 par graph x-axis ko sirf touch karta hai
questions.explanation: Leading term −x³ hai (degree 3, coefficient −1), to x → ∞ par p(x) → −∞ — ye sahi hai. −1 ki multiplicity 2 (even) hai, to wahan graph sirf touch karta hai, cross nahi. 3 ki multiplicity 1 (odd) hai, to wahan cross karta hai. x = −2 par p = −(1)(−5) = 5 > 0, to x < −1 me p(x) positive hai, negative nahi.

weeks.title: One-one, onto and inverse
weeks.summary: Functions ko one-one, onto aur bijective ke hisaab se check karna, inverse nikalna, composition aur graph shifts samajhna.
concepts: **One-one (injective)**: alag inputs ke alag outputs; f(a) = f(b) ⇒ a = b. Graph pe **horizontal line test**: koi bhi horizontal line graph ko ek se zyada baar na kaate.
**Onto (surjective)**: codomain ka har element kisi na kisi input ka output ho, yaani range = codomain.
**Bijective** = one-one + onto. Sirf bijective function ka **inverse** f⁻¹ exist karta hai.
**Inverse nikalne ka tarika**: y = f(x) likho, x ko y ke terms me solve karo, phir x aur y swap karo. Dhyan do: f⁻¹(x) ka matlab 1/f(x) nahi hai.
**Composition**: (g∘f)(x) = g(f(x)) — pehle f, phir g. Generally g∘f ≠ f∘g.
f⁻¹ ka graph, f ke graph ka line y = x me mirror image hota hai.
**Graph transformations**: f(x) + k graph ko k upar le jaata hai, f(x − h) graph ko h right shift karta hai, −f(x) x-axis me reflect karta hai.

example.problem: f: ℝ → ℝ, f(x) = 3x − 4. Dikhao ki f bijective hai aur f⁻¹ nikalo.
steps: One-one: f(a) = f(b) ⇒ 3a − 4 = 3b − 4 ⇒ a = b. To f one-one hai.
Onto: koi bhi y ∈ ℝ lo; x = (y + 4)/3 bhi real hai aur f(x) = y. To f onto hai.
Isliye f bijective hai aur inverse exist karta hai.
y = 3x − 4 ⇒ x = (y + 4)/3. x aur y swap karo.

mistakes: f⁻¹(x) ko 1/f(x) samajhna. Inverse function input-output ko ulta karta hai, reciprocal nahi leta.
Onto check karte waqt codomain ignore karna. f(x) = eˣ, ℝ → ℝ par onto nahi hai, par ℝ → (0, ∞) par onto hai.
Composition ka order ulta lena: (g∘f)(x) me pehle f lagta hai, g baad me.
revision: f(x − h) + k: h right, k up.

questions.question: f: ℝ → ℝ, f(x) = x². Ye function kaisa hai?
questions.explanation: f(2) = f(−2) = 4, to one-one nahi. Negative numbers (jaise −1) kabhi output nahi aate, to codomain ℝ par onto bhi nahi. Domain [0, ∞) aur codomain [0, ∞) karne par hi ye bijective banta hai.

questions.question: f(x) = 2x + 1 aur g(x) = x². (g∘f)(1) kya hai?
questions.explanation: (g∘f)(1) = g(f(1)) = g(3) = 9. 3 tab aata hai jab order ulta karke (f∘g)(1) = f(1) = 3 nikal lete ho.

questions.question: f(x) = (x − 5)/2 ka inverse function kya hai?
questions.explanation: y = (x − 5)/2 ⇒ 2y = x − 5 ⇒ x = 2y + 5. Swap karke f⁻¹(x) = 2x + 5. Check: f(f⁻¹(1)) = f(7) = 1 ✓. 2/(x − 5) reciprocal hai, inverse nahi.

questions.question: Inme se kaunsa function f: ℝ → ℝ bijective hai?
questions.explanation: x³ strictly increasing hai (one-one) aur har real number ka cube root real hai (onto). eˣ one-one hai par negative values ya 0 kabhi nahi deta, isliye ℝ par onto nahi — ye sabse common trap hai. x² aur |x| one-one hi nahi.

questions.question: y = (x − 3)² + 2 ka graph, y = x² ke graph ko kaise shift karke milta hai?
questions.explanation: f(x − 3) graph ko 3 units right le jaata hai (minus dekh kar left mat socho), aur + 2 graph ko 2 units upar. Vertex (0, 0) se (3, 2) pe chala jaata hai.

questions.question: f(x) = 2x + 3 aur g(x) = x − 1. (f∘g)⁻¹(7) kya hai?
questions.explanation: (f∘g)(x) = f(x − 1) = 2(x − 1) + 3 = 2x + 1. (f∘g)⁻¹(7) matlab wo x jiske liye 2x + 1 = 7, yaani x = 3. Doosra tarika: g⁻¹(f⁻¹(7)) = g⁻¹(2) = 3. Order ulta lene par f⁻¹(g⁻¹(7)) = 5/2 aata hai; 15 to (f∘g)(7) hai.

questions.question: f(x) = 4x − 3 hai. f⁻¹(5) kya hai?
questions.explanation: f⁻¹(5) wo input hai jiska output 5 ho: 4x − 3 = 5 ⇒ x = 2. Check: f(2) = 5 ✓. 17 to f(5) hai — inverse me input-output ulta hota hai. 1/17 = 1/f(5) reciprocal hai; f⁻¹ ka matlab 1/f nahi hota.

questions.question: f(x) = x + 4 aur g(x) = 3x. (f∘g)(x) kya hai?
questions.explanation: (f∘g)(x) = f(g(x)) = f(3x) = 3x + 4 — pehle g, phir f. 3x + 12 = g(f(x)) = 3(x + 4) hai, yaani order ulta. 3x² + 12x to f(x) · g(x) product hai, composition nahi.

questions.question: Inme se kaunsa function f: ℝ → ℝ one-one hai?
questions.explanation: 5 − 2x ek straight line hai jiska slope −2 hai; har horizontal line ise sirf ek baar kaatti hai, to one-one. Baaki teeno fail: x² + 1 me f(1) = f(−1) = 2, |x − 2| me f(0) = f(4) = 2, aur (x − 1)² me f(0) = f(2) = 1. Decreasing function bhi one-one hota hai — sirf increasing hi zaroori nahi.

questions.question: y = |x| ke graph ko transform karke y = −|x + 2| + 3 banta hai. Naye graph ka 'corner' point (vertex) kahan hai?
questions.explanation: |x + 2| = f(x − (−2)), to graph 2 units left jaata hai; − sign x-axis me reflect karta hai (V ulta ho jaata hai), aur + 3 use 3 units upar le jaata hai. Vertex (0, 0) → (−2, 0) → (−2, 3). (2, 3) me + 2 ko right shift samajh liya. Reflection vertex ko nahi hilata kyunki wo y = 0 par hai, isliye −3 wale options galat hain.

questions.question: f: ℝ → [k, ∞), f(x) = x² − 4x + 7 onto ho, iske liye k kya hona chahiye?
questions.explanation: Onto ka matlab range = codomain. Range nikalo: a = 1 > 0, vertex x = −(−4)/2 = 2, minimum f(2) = 4 − 8 + 7 = 3. Range [3, ∞), to k = 3. 2 sirf vertex ka x-coordinate hai, aur 7 = f(0) y-intercept hai — minimum value nahi.

questions.question: f(x) = (2x + 1)/(x − 3), x ≠ 3. f⁻¹(x) kya hai?
questions.explanation: y = (2x + 1)/(x − 3) ⇒ xy − 3y = 2x + 1 ⇒ x(y − 2) = 3y + 1 ⇒ x = (3y + 1)/(y − 2). Swap karke f⁻¹(x) = (3x + 1)/(x − 2). Check: f(0) = −1/3, aur f⁻¹(−1/3) = 0/(−7/3) = 0 ✓. (x − 3)/(2x + 1) reciprocal 1/f(x) hai, inverse nahi. (2x − 1)/(x + 3) me har sign ulta kar diya — rational function ka inverse aise nahi banta, x ko solve karna padta hai.

questions.question: g(x) = 3x + 2 aur f(g(x)) = 6x + 7 hai. f(x) kya hai?
questions.explanation: u = g(x) = 3x + 2 lo, to x = (u − 2)/3. f(u) = 6 · (u − 2)/3 + 7 = 2u − 4 + 7 = 2u + 3, yaani f(x) = 2x + 3. Check: f(3x + 2) = 6x + 4 + 3 = 6x + 7 ✓. 3x + 5 = (6x + 7) − (3x + 2) sirf subtract karna hai; 18x + 19 to (6x + 7) me 3x + 2 rakh diya — order ulta. 2x + 7 me −4 wala adjustment bhool gaye.

questions.question: f: [3, ∞) → [1, ∞), f(x) = x² − 6x + 10 bijective hai. f⁻¹(10) kya hai?
questions.explanation: f⁻¹(10) wo x hai jiske liye f(x) = 10: x² − 6x + 10 = 10 ⇒ x(x − 6) = 0 ⇒ x = 0 ya 6. Domain [3, ∞) hai, to sirf x = 6 valid. Inverse function ka ek hi output hota hai, isliye 'dono' galat hai — domain restrict karke hi f one-one bana tha. 50 = f(10) hai, f⁻¹(10) nahi.

questions.question: y = f(x) ke graph ko 2 units left aur 3 units neeche shift karne par y = x² + 4x + 1 ka graph milta hai. f(x) kya hai?
questions.explanation: 2 left aur 3 neeche ka matlab naya graph f(x + 2) − 3 hai. To f(x + 2) − 3 = x² + 4x + 1 = (x + 2)² − 3, yaani f(x + 2) = (x + 2)², isliye f(x) = x². Ulta karke bhi: naye graph ko 2 right aur 3 upar le jao: (x − 2 + 2)² − 3 + 3 = x² ✓. (x + 4)² tab aata hai jab wapas jaate waqt bhi left shift kar dete ho; x² − 6 me vertical shift ki direction galat hai, aur x² + 4x + 4 me horizontal shift undo hi nahi kiya.

weeks.title: Exponentials and logarithms
weeks.summary: Exponential growth/decay functions, logarithm as inverse, log ke rules, aur exponential/log equations solve karna.
concepts: **Exponential function**: f(x) = aˣ, jahan a > 0 aur a ≠ 1. Domain ℝ, range (0, ∞), aur graph hamesha (0, 1) se guzarta hai.
a > 1 ho to function increasing (**growth**), 0 < a < 1 ho to decreasing (**decay**).
**Exponent rules**: aᵐ · aⁿ = aᵐ⁺ⁿ, aᵐ / aⁿ = aᵐ⁻ⁿ, (aᵐ)ⁿ = aᵐⁿ, a⁰ = 1, a⁻ⁿ = 1/aⁿ.
**Logarithm**: logₐ(x) = y ka matlab aʸ = x. Log, exponential ka inverse hai; iska domain (0, ∞) hai aur logₐ(1) = 0.
**Log rules**: log(xy) = log x + log y, log(x/y) = log x − log y, log(xⁿ) = n · log x. Par log(x + y) ka koi aisa rule nahi hai.
**Change of base**: logₐ(x) = ln(x) / ln(a). **ln** natural log hai jiska base e ≈ 2.718 hai.
Growth model: A = P(1 + r)ᵗ. Kitne time me value double hogi, ye log se nikalte hain.

steps: Domain check: x > 0 aur x − 2 > 0, to x > 2 chahiye.
Product rule: log₂(x(x − 2)) = 3.
Exponential form: x(x − 2) = 2³ = 8.
x = −2 domain (x > 2) me nahi hai, isliye reject.
Check: log₂4 + log₂2 = 2 + 1 = 3 ✓. Answer: **x = 4**.

mistakes: log(x + y) = log x + log y likh dena. Rule product ke liye hai: log(xy) = log x + log y.
Log equation solve karke domain check na karna — negative ya zero ka log defined nahi hota, aise roots reject karo.
logₐ(x) aur logₓ(a) ko same samajhna; ye ek doosre ke reciprocal hain.
revision: log(xy) = log x + log y; log(xⁿ) = n log x.
aˣ ki range (0, ∞); log ka domain (0, ∞).

questions.question: log₂(64) ki value kya hai?
questions.explanation: 2⁶ = 64, isliye log₂(64) = 6. 8 tab aata hai jab √64 le lete ho, aur 32 jab 64/2 kar dete ho — log ka matlab 'kaunsi power' hai.

questions.question: f(x) = (1/2)ˣ ke baare me kaunsa statement sahi hai?
options: Iski range (0, ∞) hai aur ye decreasing hai
Iski range saare real numbers hai
questions.explanation: Base 1/2 < 1 hai, isliye function decreasing hai, aur aˣ hamesha positive hota hai, to range (0, ∞). Graph (0, 1) se guzarta hai, (1, 0) se nahi — (1, 0) to log graph ka point hai.

questions.question: log₁₀(50) + log₁₀(2) ki value kya hai?
questions.explanation: Product rule: log(50) + log(2) = log(100) = 2, kyunki 10² = 100. log(52) trap hai — logs add karne par numbers multiply hote hain, add nahi. 100 andar wali value hai, log nahi.

questions.question: Solve karo: 3^(2x − 1) = 27.
questions.explanation: 27 = 3³, to 2x − 1 = 3, 2x = 4, x = 2. Check: 3³ = 27 ✓. x = 14 tab aata hai jab 2x − 1 = 27 likh dete ho (base same karna bhool gaye); 3/2 tab jab −1 ignore kar diya.

questions.question: log₄(8) ki value kya hai?
questions.explanation: 4ʸ = 8 ⇒ 2^(2y) = 2³ ⇒ 2y = 3 ⇒ y = 3/2. Change of base se bhi: log₂8 / log₂4 = 3/2. 2/3 tab aata hai jab fraction ulta likh dete ho, yaani log₈(4).

questions.question: Solve karo: log₃(x) + log₃(x − 8) = 2.
questions.explanation: log₃(x(x − 8)) = 2 ⇒ x² − 8x = 9 ⇒ x² − 8x − 9 = 0 ⇒ (x − 9)(x + 1) = 0. x = −1 par log₃(−1) defined nahi, isliye reject. Sirf x = 9: log₃9 + log₃1 = 2 + 0 = 2 ✓. Dono roots rakh lena main trap hai.

questions.question: (3²)³ / 3⁴ ki value kya hai?
questions.explanation: (3²)³ = 3⁶ (powers multiply hoti hain), aur 3⁶ / 3⁴ = 3⁶⁻⁴ = 3² = 9. 3 tab aata hai jab (3²)³ ko 3²⁺³ = 3⁵ le lete ho. 81 tab jab (3²)³ ko 3^(2³) = 3⁸ samajh lete ho, aur 1/9 me division ulta ho gaya.

questions.question: log₅(1/125) ki value kya hai?
questions.explanation: 1/125 = 1/5³ = 5⁻³, to log₅(1/125) = −3. 3 = log₅(125) hai — 1/125 ka matlab negative power. 1/3 aur −1/3 tab aate hain jab log ko 'kitne se divide' samajh lete ho; log power batata hai.

questions.question: f(x) = log₂(x − 4) ka domain kya hai?
questions.explanation: Log sirf positive number ka defined hota hai, to x − 4 > 0, yaani x > 4. x ≥ 4 galat hai kyunki x = 4 par log₂(0) aata hai, jo defined nahi. x > 0 tab aata hai jab andar wala − 4 ignore kar dete ho.

questions.question: log₂(3) · log₃(16) ki value kya hai?
questions.explanation: Change of base: log₂(3) = ln 3/ln 2 aur log₃(16) = ln 16/ln 3. Product = ln 16/ln 2 = log₂(16) = 4 — ln 3 cancel ho jaata hai. log₂ 48 tab aata hai jab logs ke product ko log of product (3 · 16) samajh lete ho, jo rule sirf log(xy) = log x + log y ke liye hai. 16 andar wali value hai, log nahi.

questions.question: Ek town ki population 2000 hai aur har saal 10% badhti hai (compound growth). 2 saal baad population kitni hogi?
questions.explanation: A = P(1 + r)ᵗ = 2000 · (1.1)² = 2000 · 1.21 = 2420. 2400 tab aata hai jab har saal sirf original 2000 ka 10% (200) jodte ho — wo simple growth hai, exponential nahi. 2200 sirf 1 saal baad ki population hai.

questions.question: Ek medicine ki body me quantity har 4 ghante me aadhi ho jaati hai. 800 mg se 50 mg tak aane me kitne ghante lagenge?
questions.explanation: Quantity = 800 · (1/2)^(t/4). 800 · (1/2)^(t/4) = 50 ⇒ (1/2)^(t/4) = 1/16 = (1/2)⁴ ⇒ t/4 = 4 ⇒ t = 16 ghante. Steps se bhi: 800 → 400 → 200 → 100 → 50, yaani 4 halvings × 4 ghante. 4 sirf halvings ki count hai, ghante nahi; 12 me ek halving kam gini. 64 tab aata hai jab 800/50 = 16 ko halvings ki count maan kar 4 se multiply kar dete ho.

questions.question: Equation 4ˣ − 6 · 2ˣ + 8 = 0 ke saare solutions kya hain?
questions.explanation: 4ˣ = (2ˣ)², to u = 2ˣ rakho: u² − 6u + 8 = 0 ⇒ (u − 2)(u − 4) = 0 ⇒ u = 2 ya 4. 2ˣ = 2 ⇒ x = 1, aur 2ˣ = 4 ⇒ x = 2. Dono valid hain kyunki 2 aur 4 positive hain (2ˣ hamesha positive hota hai). 'x = 2 ya x = 4' me u ki values ko hi x likh diya — wapas 2ˣ = u solve karna padta hai.

questions.question: Solve karo: log₂(x) + log₄(x) = 6.
questions.explanation: Base same karo: log₄(x) = log₂(x)/log₂(4) = log₂(x)/2. To log₂x + (1/2)log₂x = 6 ⇒ (3/2)log₂x = 6 ⇒ log₂x = 4 ⇒ x = 16. Check: log₂16 + log₄16 = 4 + 2 = 6 ✓. x = 8 tab aata hai jab log₄ ko bhi log₂ maan lete ho (2 log₂x = 6). x = 4 tab jab log₄x = 2 log₂x likh dete ho (fraction ulta), aur x = 64 me doosra term chhoot gaya.

questions.question: Agar log₁₀2 = a aur log₁₀3 = b, to log₁₀(7.2) kya hai?
questions.explanation: 7.2 = 72/10 = (2³ · 3²)/10. To log(7.2) = 3 log 2 + 2 log 3 − log 10 = 3a + 2b − 1. '3a + 2b' log 72 hai — /10 wala −1 bhool gaye. 2a + 3b − 1 me powers ulti lag gayi (72 = 2³ · 3², 2² · 3³ nahi). 6ab − 1 me log ke andar ka product logs ka product samajh liya, jabki log(xy) = log x + log y hota hai.

weeks.title: Sequences and limits
weeks.summary: AP aur GP ke formulas, sequence ka convergence, function ke limits nikalne ke tarike, aur continuity ka matlab.
concepts: **Sequence**: numbers ki ordered list a₁, a₂, a₃, ..., jise nth term formula aₙ se describe karte hain.
**AP (Arithmetic Progression)**: aₙ = a + (n − 1)d, aur first n terms ka sum Sₙ = (n/2)[2a + (n − 1)d].
**GP (Geometric Progression)**: aₙ = a · rⁿ⁻¹. |r| < 1 ho to infinite sum = a/(1 − r); |r| ≥ 1 par infinite sum finite nahi hota.
**Convergent sequence**: n → ∞ par aₙ kisi fixed number L ke paas pahunchta hai, jaise 1/n → 0. Warna **divergent**, jaise aₙ = n ya (−1)ⁿ.
**Limit of a function**: lim(x→a) f(x) = L matlab x ko a ke bahut kareeb le jao to f(x), L ke kareeb aata hai. Left-hand aur right-hand limits equal hone chahiye.
**0/0 form**: seedha value rakhne par 0/0 aaye to factorise karke common factor cancel karo, phir value rakho.
**x → ∞ par rational function**: numerator aur denominator ko highest power se divide karo. Degrees equal hon to limit = leading coefficients ka ratio.
**Continuity**: f, x = a par continuous hai agar lim(x→a) f(x) exist kare aur f(a) ke barabar ho.

steps: Seedha x = 3 rakho: (9 − 9)/(3 − 3) = 0/0, ye indeterminate form hai.
Numerator factorise karo: x² − 9 = (x − 3)(x + 3).
x → 3 me x ≠ 3, isliye (x − 3) cancel kar sakte hain: expression = x + 3.
Ab x = 3 rakho: 3 + 3 = 6.
Answer: limit = **6**. (Function x = 3 par defined nahi hai, phir bhi limit exist karti hai.)

mistakes: 0/0 aate hi 'limit exist nahi karti' bol dena. 0/0 ka matlab hai aur kaam karo — factorise ya simplify karo.
AP ka nth term a + nd likh dena. Sahi hai a + (n − 1)d, kyunki pehle term me d add nahi hota.
|r| ≥ 1 wali GP par bhi a/(1 − r) laga dena — ye formula sirf |r| < 1 ke liye hai.
revision: GP: aₙ = a·rⁿ⁻¹, S∞ = a/(1 − r) for |r| < 1.
Continuous at a: LHL = RHL = f(a).

questions.question: AP 4, 7, 10, ... ka 10th term kya hai?
questions.explanation: a = 4, d = 3: a₁₀ = 4 + (10 − 1)·3 = 4 + 27 = 31. 34 tab aata hai jab a + nd = 4 + 30 use kar lete ho.

questions.question: lim(n→∞) 1/n kya hai?
questions.explanation: n jitna bada hota hai, 1/n utna 0 ke paas jaata hai (1/1000, 1/1000000, ...). Ye kabhi exactly 0 nahi banta, par limit 0 hi hai — limit me 'kareeb pahunchna' hi kaafi hai.

questions.question: lim(x→2) (x² − 4)/(x − 2) kya hai?
questions.explanation: Seedha rakhne par 0/0. x² − 4 = (x − 2)(x + 2), cancel karke x + 2, aur x = 2 par 4. 0/0 dekh kar 'limit exist nahi karti' bolna galat hai.

questions.question: Infinite GP 6 + 3 + 3/2 + 3/4 + ... ka sum kya hai?
questions.explanation: a = 6, r = 1/2 (|r| < 1). S∞ = 6/(1 − 1/2) = 6/(1/2) = 12. 10.5 sirf pehle teen terms ka sum hai, aur infinite terms ka matlab infinite sum nahi hota jab r chhota ho.

questions.question: lim(x→∞) (3x² + 5)/(2x² − x) kya hai?
questions.explanation: Upar-neeche x² se divide karo: (3 + 5/x²)/(2 − 1/x). x → ∞ par 5/x² → 0 aur 1/x → 0, to limit = 3/2. Degrees equal hain, isliye answer leading coefficients ka ratio hai — 0 ya ∞ nahi.

questions.question: f(x) = x + 1 jab x < 1, aur f(x) = 3x − k jab x ≥ 1. f, x = 1 par continuous ho, iske liye k kya hona chahiye?
questions.explanation: Left-hand limit = 1 + 1 = 2. Right side aur f(1) = 3 − k. Continuity ke liye 3 − k = 2, to k = 1. k = 2 tab aata hai jab LHL hi ko k samajh lete ho.

questions.question: GP 3, 6, 12, 24, ... ka 6th term kya hai?
questions.explanation: a = 3, r = 2: a₆ = a · r⁵ = 3 · 32 = 96. 192 = 3 · 2⁶ tab aata hai jab power n − 1 ki jagah n le lete ho. 18 = 3 + 5 · 3 AP wala formula hai — GP me har step pe multiply hota hai, add nahi.

questions.question: AP 2, 5, 8, 11, ... ke pehle 20 terms ka sum kya hai?
questions.explanation: a = 2, d = 3, n = 20: S₂₀ = (20/2)[2·2 + 19·3] = 10 · 61 = 610. 640 tab aata hai jab (n − 1)d ki jagah nd = 60 le lete ho. 1220 me n/2 ki jagah n se multiply kar diya, aur 59 to 20th term hai, sum nahi.

questions.question: Inme se kaunsa sequence convergent hai?
questions.explanation: (2n + 1)/n = 2 + 1/n, aur 1/n → 0, to ye 2 ki taraf converge karta hai. (−1)ⁿ hamesha −1 aur 1 ke beech jhoolta rehta hai, kisi ek number ke paas nahi jaata — divergent. n² aur 2ⁿ bina limit ke badhte jaate hain, to divergent.

questions.question: lim(x→∞) (5x + 3)/(x² + 1) kya hai?
questions.explanation: Upar-neeche x² se divide karo: (5/x + 3/x²)/(1 + 1/x²). x → ∞ par numerator → 0 aur denominator → 1, to limit 0. Denominator ki degree (2) badi hai, isliye neeche wala tezi se badhta hai. 5 tab aata hai jab degrees alag hone par bhi leading coefficients ka ratio le lete ho — wo rule sirf equal degrees ke liye hai.

questions.question: lim(x→1) (x² + 2x − 3)/(x² − 1) kya hai?
questions.explanation: Seedha rakhne par 0/0. Factorise karo: (x + 3)(x − 1) / ((x − 1)(x + 1)) = (x + 3)/(x + 1). Ab x = 1 rakho: 4/2 = 2. 4 tab aata hai jab cancel ke baad sirf numerator (x + 3) me value rakh dete ho. 0/0 dekh kar 'exist nahi karti' bolna galat hai — 0/0 ka matlab hai aur simplify karo.

questions.question: Ek AP ka 4th term 14 aur 9th term 34 hai. Is AP ke pehle 15 terms ka sum kya hai?
questions.explanation: a + 3d = 14 aur a + 8d = 34. Ghataane par 5d = 20, d = 4, aur a = 2. S₁₅ = (15/2)[2·2 + 14·4] = 7.5 · 60 = 450. 480 tab aata hai jab 14d ki jagah 15d le lete ho. 58 = a₁₅ hai (15th term), sum nahi, aur 900 me n/2 ki jagah n laga diya.

questions.question: Ek infinite GP ka pehla term 8 hai aur uska sum 24 hai. Is GP ka 3rd term kya hai?
questions.explanation: S∞ = a/(1 − r): 8/(1 − r) = 24 ⇒ 1 − r = 1/3 ⇒ r = 2/3 (|r| < 1 ✓). 3rd term = a · r² = 8 · 4/9 = 32/9. 16/3 = a · r doosra term hai. 2/3 to r hai, aur 8/9 tab aata hai jab 1 − r = 1/3 ko hi r = 1/3 samajh lete ho.

questions.question: f(x) = (x² − 5x + 6)/(x − 2) jab x ≠ 2, aur f(2) = k. f, x = 2 par continuous ho, iske liye k kya hona chahiye?
options: Koi bhi k kaam nahi karega
questions.explanation: Continuity ke liye f(2) = lim(x→2) f(x) chahiye. x² − 5x + 6 = (x − 2)(x − 3), to x ≠ 2 par f(x) = x − 3, aur limit = 2 − 3 = −1. Isliye k = −1. 0 tab aata hai jab sirf numerator me x = 2 rakh dete ho. 0/0 hone ka matlab ye nahi ki continuous banana impossible hai — limit exist karti hai, bas f(2) ko uske barabar rakhna hai.

questions.question: Infinite GP 9 − 6 + 4 − 8/3 + ... ka sum kya hai?
questions.explanation: r = −6/9 = −2/3, aur |r| < 1, to sum finite hai: S∞ = 9/(1 − (−2/3)) = 9/(5/3) = 27/5. 27 tab aata hai jab r ka minus sign bhool kar 9/(1 − 2/3) le lete ho. 13/3 sirf pehle 4 terms ka sum hai. Terms ke sign badalne se sum infinite nahi hota — sirf |r| < 1 dekhna hai.

weeks.title: Derivatives
weeks.summary: Derivative as rate of change aur tangent slope, differentiation rules, tangent line ki equation, aur maxima-minima nikalna.
concepts: **Derivative**: f′(x) = lim(h→0) [f(x + h) − f(x)]/h. Ye kisi point pe function ka instantaneous rate of change hai, yaani tangent line ka slope.
**Power rule**: d/dx(xⁿ) = n·xⁿ⁻¹. Constant ka derivative 0, aur d/dx(c·f) = c·f′.
**Product rule**: (uv)′ = u′v + uv′. **Quotient rule**: (u/v)′ = (u′v − uv′)/v².
**Chain rule**: d/dx f(g(x)) = f′(g(x)) · g′(x) — bahar wale ka derivative, andar wale ka derivative se multiply.
**Standard results**: (eˣ)′ = eˣ, (ln x)′ = 1/x (x > 0).
**Tangent line** x = a par: y − f(a) = f′(a)(x − a).
**Increasing/decreasing**: f′ > 0 to increasing, f′ < 0 to decreasing. **Critical points** wahan jahan f′(x) = 0.
**Second derivative test**: critical point par f″ > 0 to local minimum, f″ < 0 to local maximum.

example.problem: f(x) = x³ − 3x² + 4 ke local maximum aur local minimum nikalo.
steps: Critical points: f′(x) = 0 ⇒ x = 0 ya x = 2.
x = 0: f″(0) = −6 < 0, to local maximum; f(0) = 4.
Answer: local max **4** (x = 0 par), local min **0** (x = 2 par).

mistakes: Product ka derivative u′ · v′ likh dena. Sahi product rule u′v + uv′ hai.
Chain rule me andar wale function ka derivative multiply karna bhoolna, jaise (3x + 1)⁵ ka derivative 5(3x + 1)⁴ likh dena.
Local min/max value poochi ho to sirf x batana. Value ke liye f(x) me x rakhna padta hai.
revision: f′ = 0 and f″ > 0 ⇒ min; f″ < 0 ⇒ max.

questions.question: 4x³ − 2x + 7 ka derivative kya hai?
questions.explanation: d/dx(4x³) = 12x², d/dx(−2x) = −2, d/dx(7) = 0. Total 12x² − 2. Constant 7 ko −2 me jod dena (12x² + 5) galat hai, kyunki constant ka derivative 0 hai.

questions.question: Curve y = x² par x = 3 wale point pe tangent ka slope kya hai?
questions.explanation: Slope = f′(3), aur f′(x) = 2x, to f′(3) = 6. 9 to point ka y-coordinate f(3) hai, slope nahi.

questions.question: d/dx (x² · eˣ) kya hai?
questions.explanation: Product rule: (x²)′·eˣ + x²·(eˣ)′ = 2x·eˣ + x²·eˣ = eˣ(x² + 2x). 2x·eˣ sirf ek part hai — ye tab aata hai jab galti se (uv)′ = u′v′ jaisa kuch kar dete ho.

questions.question: d/dx (3x + 1)⁵ kya hai?
questions.explanation: Chain rule: 5(3x + 1)⁴ · d/dx(3x + 1) = 5(3x + 1)⁴ · 3 = 15(3x + 1)⁴. 5(3x + 1)⁴ me andar ka derivative 3 bhool gaye; 15(3x + 1)⁵ me power kam karna bhool gaye.

questions.question: Curve y = x² + 1 par x = 1 wale point pe tangent line ki equation kya hai?
questions.explanation: Point: f(1) = 2, to (1, 2). Slope: f′(x) = 2x, f′(1) = 2. Tangent: y − 2 = 2(x − 1) ⇒ y = 2x. Check: x = 1 par y = 2 ✓. y = 2x + 2 point (1, 2) se guzarti hi nahi.

questions.question: f(x) = 2x³ − 9x² + 12x + 1 ki local minimum value kya hai?
questions.explanation: f′(x) = 6x² − 18x + 12 = 6(x − 1)(x − 2), critical points x = 1, 2. f″(x) = 12x − 18: f″(1) = −6 (max), f″(2) = 6 (min). f(2) = 16 − 36 + 24 + 1 = 5. 6 = f(1) local maximum value hai, aur 2 to sirf min ka x-coordinate.

questions.question: 5/x² ka derivative kya hai?
questions.explanation: 5/x² = 5x⁻². Power rule: 5 · (−2) · x⁻³ = −10x⁻³ = −10/x³. 10/x³ me negative power ka minus sign chhoot gaya. −10/x me power ek ki jagah do kam kar di; power rule me power sirf 1 se kam hoti hai (−2 → −3).

questions.question: f(x) = 3eˣ + ln x hai. f′(1) kya hai?
questions.explanation: f′(x) = 3eˣ + 1/x, to f′(1) = 3e + 1. 3e tab aata hai jab ln x ka derivative bhool jaate ho (ya ln 1 = 0 dekh kar use 0 maan lete ho — par derivative 1/x hai, jo x = 1 par 1 hai). e + 1 me constant 3 chhoot gaya.

questions.question: f(x) = x² − 6x kis interval me increasing hai?
questions.explanation: f′(x) = 2x − 6. Increasing ke liye f′(x) > 0: 2x − 6 > 0 ⇒ x > 3. x < 3 me f′ < 0 hai, to wahan decreasing. x > 6 tab aata hai jab roots 0 aur 6 dekh kar sochte ho — increasing/decreasing f′ ke sign se decide hota hai, f ke roots se nahi.

questions.question: d/dx [x/(x + 1)] kya hai?
questions.explanation: Quotient rule: (u′v − uv′)/v² = (1 · (x + 1) − x · 1)/(x + 1)² = 1/(x + 1)². −1/(x + 1)² tab aata hai jab numerator me order ulta (uv′ − u′v) le lete ho. 1 = u′/v′ hai, jo quotient rule nahi. (2x + 1)/(x + 1)² me minus ki jagah plus laga diya.

questions.question: f(x) = e^(x²) hai. f′(1) kya hai?
questions.explanation: Chain rule: f′(x) = e^(x²) · d/dx(x²) = 2x · e^(x²). x = 1 par 2 · e¹ = 2e. e tab aata hai jab andar wale x² ka derivative (2x) multiply karna bhool jaate ho — eˣ ka derivative eˣ hai, par e^(x²) ka sirf e^(x²) nahi.

questions.question: Curve y = x² − 4x + 1 ke kis point par tangent, line y = 2x + 5 ke parallel hai?
questions.explanation: Parallel ka matlab tangent ka slope 2: y′ = 2x − 4 = 2 ⇒ x = 3. y = 9 − 12 + 1 = −2, to point (3, −2). (1, −2) bhi curve par hai, par wahan slope 2·1 − 4 = −2 hai — slope ka sign galat le liya. (2, −3) vertex hai jahan slope 0 hai, aur (3, 2) me y nikalne me sign ki galti.

questions.question: 12 cm × 12 cm ki square sheet ke chaaron corners se x cm side ke square kaat kar, sides mod kar ek open box banaya jaata hai. Box ka maximum possible volume kitna hai (cm³ me)?
questions.explanation: Base (12 − 2x) × (12 − 2x), height x: V(x) = x(12 − 2x)², 0 < x < 6. V′(x) = (12 − 2x)² − 4x(12 − 2x) = (12 − 2x)(12 − 6x) = 0 ⇒ x = 2 (x = 6 par V = 0). V(2) = 2 · 8² = 128. Second derivative ya values check karo: V(1) = 100, V(3) = 108, dono kam. 2 sirf x hai, volume nahi; 64 base area hai, height se multiply karna bhool gaye. 108 = V(3) tab aata hai jab bina derivative ke x = 3 guess kar lete ho.

questions.question: Curve y = x³ − 2x par x = 2 wale point pe tangent line kheenchi jaati hai. Ye tangent y-axis ko kahan kaatti hai (y-intercept)?
questions.explanation: Point: f(2) = 8 − 4 = 4, to (2, 4). Slope: f′(x) = 3x² − 2, f′(2) = 10. Tangent: y − 4 = 10(x − 2) ⇒ y = 10x − 16, to y-intercept −16. −20 tab aata hai jab f′(x) = 3x² le lete ho (−2x ka derivative bhool gaye): y = 12x − 20. 4 to point ka y-coordinate hai, aur 16 sign ki galti hai.

questions.question: d/dx [x · (2x − 1)³] ko simplify karke kya milta hai?
questions.explanation: Product rule + chain rule: 1 · (2x − 1)³ + x · 3(2x − 1)² · 2 = (2x − 1)²[(2x − 1) + 6x] = (2x − 1)²(8x − 1). (2x − 1)²(5x − 1) tab aata hai jab chain rule me andar ka derivative 2 bhool jaate ho (6x ki jagah 3x). 6x(2x − 1)² sirf uv′ hai — product rule ka u′v part chhoot gaya.

weeks.title: Integrals
weeks.summary: Integration as reverse of differentiation, definite integral se area nikalna, substitution, aur curves ke beech ka area.
concepts: **Indefinite integral (antiderivative)**: ∫f(x) dx = F(x) + C, jahan F′(x) = f(x). Constant C mat bhoolo, kyunki constant ka derivative 0 hota hai.
**Basic rules**: ∫xⁿ dx = xⁿ⁺¹/(n + 1) + C (n ≠ −1), ∫(1/x) dx = ln|x| + C, ∫eˣ dx = eˣ + C.
**Linearity**: ∫[a·f(x) + b·g(x)] dx = a∫f dx + b∫g dx.
**Definite integral**: ∫ₐᵇ f(x) dx = F(b) − F(a). Ye **Fundamental Theorem of Calculus** hai; isme C cancel ho jaata hai.
**Area meaning**: f ≥ 0 ho to ∫ₐᵇ f(x) dx, x = a se b tak curve ke neeche ka area hai. x-axis ke neeche wala hissa negative contribute karta hai.
**Riemann sum**: area ko patle rectangles me todkar approx karte hain; rectangles jitne patle, approximation utna exact.
**Area between curves**: ∫ₐᵇ [upper(x) − lower(x)] dx.
**Substitution**: ∫f(g(x))·g′(x) dx me u = g(x) rakho, to ye ∫f(u) du ban jaata hai.

example.problem: Curve y = x² + 1 ke neeche, x = 0 se x = 2 tak ka area nikalo.
steps: x² + 1 hamesha positive hai, to area = ∫₀² (x² + 1) dx.
Antiderivative: F(x) = x³/3 + x.
Answer: area = **14/3 square units** (≈ 4.67).

mistakes: Indefinite integral me + C chhod dena.
Integration me power badhane ke baad (n + 1) se divide karna bhool jaana, jaise ∫x² dx = x³ likh dena.
x-axis ke neeche wale hisse ko bhi positive area maan kar definite integral ka answer dena — definite integral net signed area deta hai.
revision: ∫(1/x) dx = ln|x| + C; ∫eˣ dx = eˣ + C.
Substitution: u = g(x), du = g′(x) dx.

questions.question: ∫(6x² + 2) dx kya hai?
questions.explanation: ∫6x² dx = 6·x³/3 = 2x³, ∫2 dx = 2x. Total 2x³ + 2x + C. 12x to derivative hai, integral nahi. 6x³ me 3 se divide karna bhool gaye.

questions.question: ∫₀³ 2x dx ki value kya hai?
questions.explanation: Antiderivative x², to 3² − 0² = 9. Geometry se bhi: base 3, height 6 wala triangle, area = (1/2)·3·6 = 9. 6 = f(3) hai, integral nahi; 18 tab aata hai jab 1/2 bhool jaate ho.

questions.question: ∫₁ᵉ (1/x) dx ki value kya hai?
questions.explanation: ∫(1/x) dx = ln x. ln(e) − ln(1) = 1 − 0 = 1. e − 1 tab aata hai jab galti se ∫(1/x) dx = x maan lete ho.

questions.question: x = 0 se x = 1 tak curves y = x aur y = x² ke beech ka area kitna hai?
questions.explanation: 0 < x < 1 me x ≥ x², to upper = x, lower = x². Area = ∫₀¹ (x − x²) dx = 1/2 − 1/3 = 1/6. 5/6 tab aata hai jab dono areas subtract ki jagah add kar dete ho.

questions.question: ∫ 2x(x² + 1)³ dx kya hai?
questions.explanation: u = x² + 1, du = 2x dx. Integral = ∫u³ du = u⁴/4 + C = (x² + 1)⁴/4 + C. Check: derivative = 4(x² + 1)³·2x/4 = 2x(x² + 1)³ ✓. 2x ko bahar rakhna galat hai, wo to du me absorb ho gaya.

questions.question: ∫₋₁² (x² − 2x) dx ki value kya hai?
questions.explanation: F(x) = x³/3 − x². F(2) = 8/3 − 4 = −4/3, F(−1) = −1/3 − 1 = −4/3. F(2) − F(−1) = 0. Function −1 se 0 tak positive (area 4/3) aur 0 se 2 tak negative (area 4/3) hai, dono cancel. 8/3 total geometric area hai, definite integral nahi.

questions.question: ∫(1/x + eˣ) dx kya hai?
questions.explanation: ∫(1/x) dx = ln|x| aur ∫eˣ dx = eˣ, to answer ln|x| + eˣ + C. −1/x² to 1/x ka derivative hai, integral nahi. eˣ⁺¹/(x + 1) me eˣ par power rule laga diya — power rule sirf xⁿ ke liye hai, aur 1/x (n = −1) uska exception hai.

questions.question: ∫₁² 3x² dx ki value kya hai?
questions.explanation: Antiderivative x³ hai (3 · x³/3). F(2) − F(1) = 8 − 1 = 7. 8 tab aata hai jab lower limit wala F(1) subtract karna bhool jaate ho. 21 = 24 − 3 tab aata hai jab 3x² ka integral 3x³ likh dete ho (3 se divide nahi kiya). 12 = 3 · 2² to function ki value hai, integral nahi.

questions.question: F′(x) = 4x aur F(0) = 3 hai. F(2) kya hai?
questions.explanation: F(x) = ∫4x dx = 2x² + C. F(0) = C = 3, to F(x) = 2x² + 3 aur F(2) = 8 + 3 = 11. 8 tab aata hai jab + C (yaani 3) chhod dete ho. 19 = 4 · 4 + 3 me power badhane ke baad 2 se divide karna bhool gaye.

questions.question: x = 0 se x = 3 tak line y = x − 1 aur x-axis ke beech ka total area (geometric area, har hissa positive) kitna hai?
questions.explanation: Line x = 1 par x-axis ko kaatti hai. 0 se 1 tak wo neeche hai: area 1/2 (triangle, base 1, height 1). 1 se 3 tak upar hai: area 2 (base 2, height 2). Total area = 1/2 + 2 = 5/2. 3/2 = ∫₀³ (x − 1) dx net signed area hai, jisme neeche wala hissa minus ho jaata hai. 2 me sirf upar wala hissa liya.

questions.question: ∫ 3x² · e^(x³) dx kya hai?
questions.explanation: u = x³ rakho, du = 3x² dx. Integral = ∫eᵘ du = eᵘ + C = e^(x³) + C. Check: d/dx e^(x³) = e^(x³) · 3x² ✓. 3e^(x³) me 3 do baar gin liya — wo to du me absorb ho chuka hai. e^(x³)/(3x²) me andar ke derivative se divide kar diya, jo substitution ka tarika nahi hai.

questions.question: Curves y = 4 − x² aur y = x + 2 ke beech band hue region ka area kitna hai?
questions.explanation: Intersection: 4 − x² = x + 2 ⇒ x² + x − 2 = 0 ⇒ x = −2, 1. Beech me parabola upar hai (x = 0 par 4 > 2). Area = ∫₋₂¹ [(4 − x²) − (x + 2)] dx = ∫₋₂¹ (2 − x − x²) dx = [2x − x²/2 − x³/3] from −2 to 1 = 7/6 − (−10/3) = 9/2. −9/2 tab aata hai jab upper − lower ki jagah lower − upper le lete ho (area negative nahi ho sakta). 7/6 me sirf upper limit wali value li, aur 27/2 me dono curves ko subtract ki jagah jod diya.

questions.question: ∫₀² x/(x² + 1) dx ki value kya hai?
questions.explanation: u = x² + 1, du = 2x dx, to x dx = du/2. Limits: x = 0 ⇒ u = 1, x = 2 ⇒ u = 5. Integral = (1/2)∫₁⁵ (1/u) du = (1/2)(ln 5 − ln 1) = (1/2) ln 5. ln 5 tab aata hai jab du = 2x dx ka 1/2 bhool jaate ho, aur 2 ln 5 me 2 se divide ki jagah multiply kar diya. 2/5 to sirf x = 2 par function ki value hai.

questions.question: k > 0 hai aur ∫₀ᵏ (2x + 1) dx = 12. k ki value kya hai?
questions.explanation: ∫₀ᵏ (2x + 1) dx = [x² + x]₀ᵏ = k² + k. k² + k = 12 ⇒ k² + k − 12 = 0 ⇒ (k + 4)(k − 3) = 0 ⇒ k = 3 ya −4. k > 0 hai, to k = 3. Check: 9 + 3 = 12 ✓. −4 condition k > 0 tod deta hai. 2√3 tab aata hai jab + 1 ka integral (x) bhool kar k² = 12 le lete ho, aur 4 factor ke sign ki galti hai.

questions.question: ∫₀⁵ f(x) dx = 10 aur ∫₀² f(x) dx = 4 hai. ∫₂⁵ [3f(x) + 2] dx kya hai?
questions.explanation: F antiderivative ho to ∫₂⁵ f = F(5) − F(2) = [F(5) − F(0)] − [F(2) − F(0)] = 10 − 4 = 6. Linearity: ∫₂⁵ [3f + 2] dx = 3 · 6 + 2 · (5 − 2) = 18 + 6 = 24. 20 tab aata hai jab constant 2 ko interval ki length se multiply nahi karte, aur 18 me + 2 wala hissa hi chhoot gaya. 36 = 3 · 10 + 6 me galti se poora ∫₀⁵ le liya.

weeks.title: Graphs, BFS and DFS
weeks.summary: Graph ki basic language, adjacency matrix/list representation, aur graph explore karne ke do tarike — BFS aur DFS — plus DAG me topological order.
concepts: **Graph** G = (V, E): V vertices (nodes) ka set aur E edges (connections) ka set. **Directed graph** me edge u → v ki direction hoti hai.
**Degree**: vertex se judi edges ki count. **Handshaking lemma**: saari degrees ka sum = 2|E|, kyunki har edge do vertices ki degree me count hoti hai.
**Adjacency matrix**: n × n matrix, A[i][j] = 1 agar i se j edge hai. Undirected graph ki matrix symmetric hoti hai.
**Adjacency list**: har vertex ke neighbours ki list. Kam edges wale (sparse) graphs me ye memory bachati hai.
**Complete graph Kₙ**: har pair ke beech edge, total n(n − 1)/2 edges.
**BFS (Breadth First Search)**: queue use karta hai aur level-by-level explore karta hai. Unweighted graph me start se har vertex tak minimum edges wala path deta hai.
**DFS (Depth First Search)**: stack ya recursion use karta hai; ek raaste me jitna deep ja sake jaata hai, phir backtrack karta hai.
**DAG** (directed acyclic graph) ke vertices ko **topological order** me rakh sakte hain: har edge u → v ke liye u, v se pehle aaye.

example.problem: Undirected graph ki edges: A–B, A–C, B–D, C–D, D–E. A se BFS chalao (neighbours alphabetical order me) aur har vertex ka level batao.
steps: Queue = [A], A visited, level(A) = 0.
A nikalo: neighbours B, C add karo. Queue = [B, C], level 1.
B nikalo: neighbour D naya hai, add karo. Queue = [C, D], level(D) = 2.
C nikalo: D pehle hi visited hai, skip. Queue = [D].
D nikalo: E naya hai, add karo, level(E) = 3. Queue = [E].
E nikalo: koi naya neighbour nahi. Queue khaali.
Answer: BFS order **A, B, C, D, E**; levels A = 0, B = C = 1, D = 2, E = 3. A se E tak minimum 3 edges.

mistakes: BFS aur DFS ke data structures mix karna: BFS → queue (FIFO), DFS → stack/recursion (LIFO).
Handshaking lemma me degree sum ko hi edges ki count maan lena — edges = degree sum / 2.
Visited mark na karna, jisse ek vertex queue me do baar aa jaata hai ya cycle me infinite loop.
revision: Undirected adjacency matrix me 1s ki count = 2|E|.
BFS = queue = levels = unweighted shortest path.
DFS = stack/recursion = deep first, then backtrack.
Topological order sirf DAG me possible.

questions.question: Ek undirected graph me 6 vertices hain jinki degrees 2, 3, 3, 2, 4, 2 hain. Graph me kitni edges hain?
questions.explanation: Degree sum = 2 + 3 + 3 + 2 + 4 + 2 = 16 = 2|E|, to |E| = 8. 16 degree sum hai, edges nahi — har edge do baar count hoti hai.

questions.question: BFS graph explore karne ke liye mainly kaunsa data structure use karta hai?
questions.explanation: BFS queue (first in, first out) use karta hai, isliye pehle paas wale (level 1) vertices process hote hain, phir level 2. Stack DFS ke liye hai; priority queue Dijkstra jaise algorithms me aata hai.

questions.question: Complete graph K₆ me kitni edges hain?
questions.explanation: Har pair ke beech ek edge: 6·5/2 = 15. 30 tab aata hai jab 2 se divide nahi karte, yaani har edge ko do baar gin lete ho.

questions.question: Undirected graph ki edges: 1–2, 1–3, 2–4, 3–4, 4–5. Vertex 1 se recursive DFS chalao, neighbours ascending order me. Visit order kya hoga?
questions.explanation: 1 → sabse chhota neighbour 2 → 2 ka unvisited neighbour 4 → 4 ke neighbours 2, 3, 5 me pehla unvisited 3 → 3 ke saare neighbours visited, backtrack to 4 → 5. Order 1, 2, 4, 3, 5. 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 BFS ka order hai, DFS ka nahi.

questions.question: 5 vertices aur 7 edges wale undirected simple graph ki adjacency matrix me kitne 1s honge?
questions.explanation: Undirected edge i–j matrix me do jagah 1 deti hai: A[i][j] aur A[j][i]. Isliye 1s = 2 · 7 = 14. 7 tab aata hai jab symmetry bhool jaate ho; 25 to poori matrix ke cells hain.

questions.question: DAG ki edges: A → B, A → C, B → D, C → D, D → E. Inme se kaunsa valid topological order hai?
questions.explanation: Har edge u → v me u pehle aana chahiye. A, C, B, D, E me saari edges follow hoti hain (B aur C ka aapas me order free hai). Pehle option me C → D tootta hai (D, C se pehle), doosre me A → B, aur chauthe me D → E.

questions.question: Ek undirected graph ki adjacency matrix neeche di gayi hai. Vertex 3 ki degree kya hai?
questions.explanation: Undirected graph me vertex ki degree = uski row me 1s ki count. Row 3: 1, 1, 0, 1, to degree 3 (vertex 3 ke neighbours 1, 2, 4). 4 tab aata hai jab row ke saare cells gin lete ho, 0 wale bhi. 10 poori matrix ke 1s hain, jo saari degrees ka sum (2|E|) hai.

questions.question: Ek unweighted graph me start vertex se BFS chalane par kya guarantee milti hai?
options: Weighted graph me sabse kam total weight wala path
Start se har reachable vertex tak minimum edges wala path
Vertices hamesha alphabetical order me visit hote hain
Graph me koi cycle nahi hai
questions.explanation: BFS level-by-level chalta hai: pehle 1 edge door wale, phir 2 edge door wale. Isliye kisi vertex tak pehli baar pahunchne wala path minimum edges ka hota hai. Weights hon to ye guarantee nahi rehti — uske liye Dijkstra jaisa algorithm chahiye. Visit order neighbours ke order par depend karta hai, aur BFS cycle hone na hone ka koi guarantee nahi deta.

questions.question: Topological order kis type ke graph me possible hai?
options: Directed graph me jisme kam se kam ek cycle ho
questions.explanation: Topological order me har edge u → v ke liye u, v se pehle aana chahiye. Agar cycle ho, jaise A → B → C → A, to A ko B se pehle aur B ke baad dono aana padega — impossible. Isliye sirf DAG me topological order hota hai. Undirected graph me edges ki direction hi nahi hoti, to 'pehle-baad' ki condition ka matlab hi nahi banta.

questions.question: Ek complete graph Kₙ me 28 edges hain. Isme kitne vertices hain?
questions.explanation: Kₙ me n(n − 1)/2 edges: n(n − 1)/2 = 28 ⇒ n(n − 1) = 56 = 8 · 7, to n = 8. 7 vertices par sirf 7 · 6/2 = 21 edges hoti hain. 56 = n(n − 1) hai, n nahi, aur 14 = 28/2 me formula ka galat istemal hai.

questions.question: Undirected graph ki edges: S–A, S–B, A–C, B–C, C–D, D–E, B–F, F–E. S se BFS chalao. Vertex E ka level (S se minimum edges) kya hoga?
questions.explanation: Level 0: S. Level 1: A, B. Level 2: C (A/B se), F (B se). Level 3: D (C se), E (F se). To E level 3 par hai, path S → B → F → E. 4 tab aata hai jab S → A → C → D → E wala lamba path pakad lete ho (DFS jaisa soch kar). BFS sabse pehle jis level par vertex milta hai, wahi uski minimum distance hai.

questions.question: Undirected graph ki edges: A–B, A–D, B–C, B–E, D–E, C–F, E–F, D–G. A se BFS chalao, neighbours alphabetical order me queue me daalo, aur har vertex ko pehli baar milte hi visited mark karo. Visit order kya hoga?
options: A, B, D, C, E, G, F
A, B, C, F, E, D, G
A, B, D, C, E, F, G
A, B, C, E, D, G, F
questions.explanation: Queue [A]. A nikalo: B, D daalo. B nikalo: C, E daalo (A visited). D nikalo: E pehle se queue me hai, G daalo. C nikalo: F daalo. E, G, F nikalte hain, kuch naya nahi. Order: A, B, D, C, E, G, F. 'A, B, C, F, E, D, G' DFS ka order hai. 'A, B, D, C, E, F, G' me G ko F ke baad rakh diya, jabki G, D ke through level 2 par hi queue me aa gaya tha aur F level 3 par hai.

questions.question: Inme se kaunsa degree sequence kisi bhi simple undirected graph ka NAHI ho sakta?
questions.explanation: Handshaking lemma: degrees ka sum = 2|E|, jo hamesha even hota hai. (3, 3, 3, 3, 3) ka sum 15 odd hai, to aisa graph impossible. Baaki sab bante hain: (3, 3, 3, 3) = K₄, (2, 2, 2, 2, 2) = 5 vertices ki cycle, aur (1, 1, 2, 2) = 4 vertices ka path. Sirf 'sab degrees equal hain' dekh kar K₄ ya cycle ko reject karna trap hai.

questions.question: DAG ki edges: A → C, B → C, C → D, C → E. Is DAG ke kitne alag valid topological orders hain?
questions.explanation: C se pehle A aur B dono aane chahiye, aur C ke baad D aur E. To order hamesha {A, B} → C → {D, E} jaisa hai. A, B aapas me 2 tarah se aur D, E aapas me 2 tarah se: 2 × 2 = 4 orders (jaise A, B, C, D, E aur B, A, C, E, D). 2 tab aata hai jab sirf ek pair ki freedom ginte ho. 6 tab jab soch lete ho ki D ya E, C se pehle bhi aa sakte hain.

questions.question: Complete graph K₁₀ me se 7 edges hata kar ek simple undirected graph banaya gaya. Iski 10 × 10 adjacency matrix me kitne 0 honge?
questions.explanation: K₁₀ me 10 · 9/2 = 45 edges, to bache 45 − 7 = 38. Undirected edge matrix me do 1 deti hai: 1s = 2 · 38 = 76. Total cells 100, to 0s = 100 − 76 = 24 (10 diagonal + 7 · 2 = 14 hataayi gayi edges ke). 14 me diagonal ke 10 zeros bhool gaye, 17 = 10 + 7 me symmetry (har edge do cells) bhool gaye, aur 62 = 100 − 38 me 1s ki count edges ke barabar maan li.

weeks.title: Shortest paths and spanning trees
weeks.summary: Weighted graphs me shortest path (Dijkstra, Bellman-Ford) aur minimum spanning tree (Prim, Kruskal) nikalna.
concepts: **Weighted graph**: har edge pe ek weight (distance, cost, time). Path ka weight = uski edges ke weights ka sum.

**Dijkstra's algorithm**: single source se shortest paths, jab saare weights non-negative hon. Har step pe sabse kam tentative distance wala unvisited vertex finalize karo aur uske neighbours update karo.
Negative edge weights par Dijkstra galat answer de sakta hai. **Bellman-Ford** negative edges handle karta hai (agar negative cycle na ho) aur negative cycle detect bhi kar sakta hai.
**Floyd-Warshall**: saare vertex pairs ke beech shortest paths ek saath, roughly n³ steps me.
**Tree**: connected graph jisme koi cycle nahi. n vertices wale tree me exactly n − 1 edges hoti hain.
**Spanning tree**: graph ke saare vertices cover karne wala tree. **Minimum spanning tree (MST)** wo spanning tree jiska total weight sabse kam ho.
